detail.abstract: The healthcare industry, stagnant in productivity and overburdened by administrative tasks, stands to benefit greatly from artificial intelligence (AI) tools. Understandably, AI in healthcare has been met with skepticism and regulatory scrutiny, especially in the face of potential ethical issues. This paper examines the ethical implications of AI in healthcare as it applies to three primary use cases: automating administrative tasks, augmenting clinical practice, and automatic specific care elements. First, recent organizational actions will be examined and critiqued. Then, the four main principles of bioethics will be discussed using clinical case examples. These patient scenarios will highlight specific use cases for AI in healthcare, challenges for ethical implementation, and their potential solutions. To achieve a more efficient, effective, and convenient health care system that benefits both patients and clinicians, deployment of AI in healthcare must be contained within ethical guardrails which remain flexible to evolve with the technology. This applies to patient consent, transparency in AI algorithms to the end user, regulatory oversight, liability framework, and dataset standards. Care should be taken to avoid comparing AI tools to unrealistic standard of perfection, but rather to the current and imperfect standard of care..

title: Hierarchical Adaptive Reward-based Reinforcement Learning Model for High-Precision Text-to-SQL Generation
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, Chengdu University of Information Technology, Chengdu University of Information Technology, Chengdu University of Information Technology, affiliation not provided to SSRN, University of Electronic Science and Technology of China (UESTC) and Chengdu University of Information Technology

detail.title: Hierarchical Adaptive Reward-based Reinforcement Learning Model for High-Precision Text-to-SQL Generation
detail.abstract: Text-to-SQL, which converts natural language questions into executable SQL queries, plays a crucial role in lowering the barrier to database querying. However, accurately understanding the semantic information in natural language questions remains challenging, as existing methods often struggle to capture deep semantic relationships between user queries and database schemas. To address this issue, this paper proposes a novel Text-to-SQL large language model, termed HART, which integrates the Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) algorithm with a hierarchical multi-dimensional reward framework. Specifically, the proposed model leverages the advantages of GRPO in handling sequential decision-making and complex state spaces, thereby enhancing semantic structure understanding and improving user intent inference. Furthermore, a multi-level reward framework is designed to evaluate SQL quality from multiple perspectives, including structural correctness, semantic consistency, and execution effectiveness, through carefully designed reward signals. In addition, we also introduce a soft adaptive length-aware reward mechanism that dynamically regulates the chain-of-thought (CoT) length, enabling the model to generate accurate SQL queries with concise and efficient reasoning. Experimental results on the Spider dataset and its variants (Spider-DK, Spider-Syn, and Spider-Realistic) demonstrate that HART consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, achieving an average absolute improvement of 4–5% in execution accuracy. Meanwhile, the proposed model reduces CoT token length by over 85%, significantly improving reasoning efficiency. These results highlight the effectiveness of HART in balancing reasoning accuracy and efficiency for complex Text-to-SQL tasks.

title: Towards Mitigating Limitations of the Softmax Layer in CNNs via Piecewise Rectification
affiliations: Zhejiang University, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Zhejiang University, Zhejiang University and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Towards Mitigating Limitations of the Softmax Layer in CNNs via Piecewise Rectification
detail.abstract: The softmax layer plays a pivotal role in guiding the learning process of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs); however, it exhibits certain inherent limitations at various stages of classification training. Small softmax outputs may direct the network to learn invalid features, consequently disrupting early training. During the mid-training stage, softmax outputs ignore shared features and uncertainty, resulting in overconfidence in the network. Large softmax outputs in the later training stage are updated slowly, hindering timely convergence and leading to overfitting. Based on these insights into the characteristics of feature learning behavior during training, three tricks are proposed to rectify the softmax output: downsizing, fuzzification, and amplification. Downsizing suppresses small softmax outputs during the early training stage, preventing the extraction of invalid features and improving feature extraction efficiency. In the mid-training stage, fuzzification introduces random adjustments through membership functions to characterize the uncertainty during training, thereby bolstering robustness and generalization. Amplification enlarges softmax outputs in the later training stage, timely reducing or stopping the continued learning of already mastered features, which accelerates convergence and prevents overfitting. These techniques are integrated into a piecewise rectification module, which systematically overcomes the limitations of softmax from the dynamic perspective throughout the training process. The proposed method is validated on classification tasks using the Case Western Reserve University (CWRU) and Paderborn University (PU) datasets. The results confirm simultaneous significant improvements in classification accuracy, training efficiency, robustness, and generalizability for CNN rectified with piecewise rectification.

title: Traffic Flow Prediction with External Temporal Information and Context-Aware Dynamic Spatial Interaction
affiliations: Shanxi University, Shanxi University, Shanxi University, Shanxi University and Shanxi University

detail.title: Traffic Flow Prediction with External Temporal Information and Context-Aware Dynamic Spatial Interaction
detail.abstract: Intelligent transportation systems rely on traffic flow prediction to optimize urban planning, manage congestion, and enhance emergency response capabilities. The key issue in traffic flow prediction is how to construct a reasonable representation of spatio-temporal features to improve prediction accuracy. Existing methods typically focus on the characteristics of the current dataset, neglecting potentially valuable information from other similar datasets. To address this issue, this paper proposes a new traffic flow prediction strategy. The core idea is to enhance the model's generalization ability by pre-training temporal features on multiple similar datasets and then transferring them to the spatial-temporal prediction model of the target dataset. Furthermore, to facilitate temporal feature pre-training, we design a novel spatio-temporal network with decoupled Spatial-Temporal components and integrated Static-Dynamic feature (ST-SDNet). Moreover, to enhance the representation of spatial features, ST-SDNet models both static and dynamic spatial interaction. In particular, during the dynamic spatial interaction modelling, the model considers both the sensor's own and its neighbouring static spatial interaction characteristics as each sensor's feature. Comparative experiments on four real-world traffic flow datasets demonstrate that the ST-SDNet model combined with pre-training techniques outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods overall. The code will be released after acceptance.

title: CDGS: ConvNeXt-Enhanced and Depth Prior-Guided Single-View 3D Gaussian Splatting
affiliations: Southwest Petroleum University, Southwest Petroleum University, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Southwest Petroleum University

detail.title: CDGS: ConvNeXt-Enhanced and Depth Prior-Guided Single-View 3D Gaussian Splatting
detail.abstract: Single-view object-level 3D reconstruction is a fundamental research topic in computer vision with wide applications in industrial scenarios. Existing implicit reconstruction methods based on neural radiance fields suffer from high computational cost and cannot achieve real-time inference. Meanwhile, feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting methods such as the baseline Splatter Image are limited by insufficient multi-scale feature representation in the encosder and the lack of explicit geometric constraints, which restricts reconstruction accuracy. To address these issues, this study proposes a two-stage enhanced single-view 3D reconstruction method, termed ConvNeXt-Enhanced and Depth Prior-Guided Single-View 3D Gaussian Splatting (CDGS). In the first stage, an enhanced encoder is constructed through multi-layer residual fusion between a pretrained ConvNeXt backbone and a native UNet encoder, improving multi-scale geometric and texture feature representation. In the second stage, a frozen Depth Anything V2 model is introduced to generate monocular depth maps, which are normalized and injected into the encoder as a fourth input channel, providing explicit geometric constraints to alleviate depth ambiguity and surface drifting artifacts. Experimental results show that the proposed method significantly outperforms the baseline Splatter Image, achieving 24.92 dB PSNR, 0.93 SSIM, and 0.063 LPIPS on the ShapeNet SRN dataset (category level) and 21.82 dB PSNR, 0.881 SSIM, and 0.107 LPIPS on the Google Scanned Objects (GSO) dataset (open-category level, trained with Objaverse), while maintaining millisecond-level end-to-end inference speed. The proposed method significantly improves reconstruction accuracy without compromising real-time performance, offering a lightweight and effective solution for feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting. This advancement holds strong potential for real-time 3D object reconstruction in industrial applications and visual display systems.

title: Income Distribution and Sectoral Pattern along Balanced Growth Path: A Two-Sector Marxian-Kaleckian Growth Model
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Income Distribution and Sectoral Pattern along Balanced Growth Path: A Two-Sector Marxian-Kaleckian Growth Model
detail.abstract: To explore the sectoral pattern of growth, inspired by the stylized facts of the Chinese economy (one of the most influential emerging industrial market economy, which exhibits some interesting sectoral patterns), we develop a two-sector Marxian-Kaleckian growth model where the profit rate and growth rate are equalized, and the capacity utilization rates converge to normal level. We find that the parameters of the investment functions and the bargaining power parameters of both sectors jointly affect the growth rate. Specifically, income distribution characterized with higher real wage rigidity (measured by a wage flexibility parameter involved in the determination of income distribution) tends to increase the relative importance of consumption goods sector on balanced growth path. In addition, higher wage rigidity also implies higher degree of wage-ledness, which in turn means that the relative importance of consumption goods sector tend to change in the same direction as degree of wage-ledness.

title: Food, Biofuels and the Environment: Is There a Virtuous Path for the EU?
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, University of Paris-Saclay and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Food, Biofuels and the Environment: Is There a Virtuous Path for the EU?
detail.abstract: Energy and food security challenges prompt a reconsideration of the complex interactions within the food-feed-fuel-environment nexus. Using an agricultural supply-side model, we assess the flexibility of the agricultural production system of the European Union in meeting the growing demand for food calories and advanced biofuels, as well as the resulting environmental impacts. We characterize a two-dimensional food/biofuel production set for the EU-28 based on a grid of targets for food calories and biofuels. Simulations are conducted under the economic and technical conditions of the 2010s. The calculation of bioenergy potential is based on the valorization of crop residues and perennial crops in terms of "farm gate" equivalent biofuel. Our results reveal substantial potential for production in both food and biofuel sectors simultaneously, without increasing environmental impacts (fertilizers, irrigation, greenhouse gas emissions) or even reducing them. We highlight what could be a "winning strategy" for the EU within a corridor defined by implicit price ratios associated with food and bioenergy production constraints. However, this strategy requires significant structural and spatial changes in agricultural land allocation. This is only achievable by substantially reducing animal production and consequently the demand for animal feed.

title: How Digital Intelligence Drives Corporate Green Innovation: Evidence from China
affiliations: Tianjin University of Finance and Economics, University of International Business and Economics, Tianjin University of Finance and Economics, affiliation not provided to SSRN and University of International Business and Economics

detail.title: How Digital Intelligence Drives Corporate Green Innovation: Evidence from China
detail.abstract: Corporate green innovation is vital for sustainable development but is often hindered by technological risk, resource constraints, and information asymmetry. As a transformative production paradigm shaped by artificial intelligence, cloud computing, and big data, digital intelligence (DI) may help overcome these barriers. This study examines the causal effect of DI on corporate green innovation. We construct a semantic-rich DI index using large language models and adopt a double machine learning framework with a shift-share instrumental variable for identification. Using data on Chinese listed firms from 2007 to 2023, we find that DI significantly promotes green innovation, especially substantive green invention patents rather than utility models, suggesting limited greenwashing concerns. Mechanism analyses show that DI works by easing financing constraints, improving resource allocation efficiency, and strengthening knowledge absorptive capacity. The effect is stronger for firms with better disclosure quality and in regions with superior digital infrastructure and innovation capacity.

title: Enhancing 3D Chip Placement through Reinforcement Learning and Surrogate Modeling
affiliations: National University of Defense Technology, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Xidian University, National University of Defense Technology and Xidian University

detail.title: Enhancing 3D Chip Placement through Reinforcement Learning and Surrogate Modeling
detail.abstract: In recent years, the development of 3D chips has garnered widespread attention due to their significant advantages in performance, power consumption, area, functionality, and cost. Driven by technological advancements and market demands, 3D chips are becoming a critical direction for future chip design. However, existing methods are based on positional coding of instances within the chip, do not take into account the complex netlist structure in 3D chips, which plays a significant role in guiding the optimization of instances placement. Therefore, a new algorithm based on reinforcement learning and surrogate models for 3D chip placement (RLSM3D) is proposed in this paper. The RLSM3D algorithm includes three main contributions: Firstly, a netlist-based state space coding and action space coding (NSAC) strategy is proposed to map the current chip placement effectively. This strategy leverages netlist data to reduce the dimensionality of the state space, providing a more comprehensive representation of the placement of the chip. Secondly, a half-perimeter wire length based surrogate model (HPWL-SM) is introduced to approximate HPWL calculations and capture the movement trends of instances within 3D chips. This model incorporates two surrogate models that enhance the efficiency of the optimization process by offering a more nuanced understanding of instance movements. Thirdly, a reinforcement learning algorithm based on Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) is developed for optimizing 3D chip placement. The PPO algorithm is designed to reduce HPWL by updating both the value and policy networks, and it innovatively integrates additional net boundary length information into the action distribution, serving as an auxiliary feature that improves the performance of algorithm. In Case 2 of the 2023 ICCAD competition, RLSM3D is pitted against other reinforcement learning approaches and multi-objective genetic algorithms. The results demonstrated that RLSM3D outperformed its competitors, achieving a 19.90% reduction in the HPWL and a 4.12% decrease in terminal costs, while also securing the best experimental results.

title: Climate Risks and Firm Value
affiliations: Central Michigan University and Central Michigan University

detail.title: Climate Risks and Firm Value
detail.abstract: Climate change introduces both physical and transition risks that could fundamentally alter firm value and asset prices, yet traditional asset-pricing models largely ignore these exposures. This study examines whether climate risk is systematically priced in equity markets and how firm-level climate initiatives shape valuation and risk-adjusted returns. Using a comprehensive panel of U.S. publicly traded firms from 2010–2024, we construct firm-specific measures of climate exposure based on textual analysis of annual reports, carbon intensity, and asset geolocation. We augment the Fama–French–Carhart framework with a climate risk factor and exploit quasi-natural experiments arising from recent U.S. climate disclosure policy shocks. We document four main findings. First, firms with credible climate initiatives exhibit significantly lower idiosyncratic risk, whereas raw emissions intensity alone does not predict residual volatility once size and time effects are controlled, providing support for this channel. Second, climate-committed firms command higher valuations and superior risk-adjusted returns. Third, regulatory shocks related to climate disclosure generate heterogeneous abnormal returns, with stronger effects for firms more exposed to climate risk. Fourth, a climate risk factor carries a significant return premium and improves the explanatory power of standard asset-pricing models. Together, these results demonstrate that climate risk is a distinct, priced source of financial risk rather than a peripheral sustainability concern. The findings have implications for asset pricing, corporate governance, and climate policy in an era of heightened regulatory uncertainty.

title: Parametrised PINNs for Water Infiltration in Unsaturated Soils
affiliations: RWTH Aachen University and RWTH Aachen University

detail.title: Parametrised PINNs for Water Infiltration in Unsaturated Soils
detail.abstract: Solving water infiltration in unsaturated soils has traditionally relied on two approaches: analytical solutions and classical numerical methods. However, the former relies on simplified assumptions which are not the case in realistic field applications, while the latter is limited by spatial and temporal discretisation which remains a major obstacle, due to mass conservation issues and convergence failures. Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) have recently gained popularity in approximating non-linear functions, as a powerful mesh-free approach, by constraining the training with physical laws and with using sparse data to mimic field sensors which generally require a certain gap to mitigate interference between sensors. Despite several successful applications on modelling this problem, larger spatio-temporal domains, root water uptake, and lack of universality remain unaddressed. This study tests the efficacy of PINNs on larger domains in an unsupervised manner, and incorporates a sink term representing uniform root architecture. Furthermore, it transforms PINNs from a fixed scenario approximator to a universal approximator. This is carried out by parametrising PINNs, where the input space becomes a continuous multi-dimensional space comprising five hydraulic parameters, alongside spatio-temporal coordinates. Training is conducted with the aid of dynamic adaptive functions,yielding an efficient surrogate model. The model results were validated against analytical solution, showing high accuracy with a Nash Sutcliffe Efficiency exceeding 0.99 in 19 out of 21 tested scenarios. The worst scenario scored NSE > 0.96, corresponding to a minor underestimation of ∼ 1.0% on the Percent Bias (PBIAS) scale. The training took about 2.3× longer than standard PINN training, and P-PINN model evaluates new scenarios almost instantly without either retraining, or preprocessing and meshing. Despite this, there were limitations shown as phase errors, which are related to spectral bias and temporal causality. Nevertheless, this study shows the practicality of P-PINNs, as an efficient universal approximator for modelling infiltration problems.

title: Social Metacognition and Coordination in Chicken Games
affiliations: University of Geneva, University of Bath - School of Management, Masaryk University, University of Roehampton and University of Bath - Department of Psychology

detail.title: Social Metacognition and Coordination in Chicken Games
detail.abstract: This study reports a laboratory experiment wherein we investigate the role of social metacognition in a Chicken game. The experiment involves rounds with recommendations---that work as a correlation mechanism---followed by rounds without recommendations. We find evidence that behavior in the rounds with recommendations is not described by the mixed-strategy Nash equilibrium. Furthermore, in the absence of recommendations, we find suggestive evidence that as the group's social metacognition increases, individuals' behavior becomes closer to the correlated equilibrium. This finding suggests that social metacognition acts "as if"' it was a correlating mechanism. Thus social metacognition could enhance decision-making and coordination in strategic interactions.

title: A Parallel Perspective on the Tool Replacement Problem ​
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: A Parallel Perspective on the Tool Replacement Problem ​
detail.abstract: This paper considers a new time-based formulation of the classical tool replacement problem with a fixed sequence of jobs. In contrast to standard models that minimize the total time or cost of individual replacements, we study a system in which tool replacements in different magazine slots can be performed in parallel. In this formulation, the delay before processing the next job is determined not by the sum, but by the maximum of the times of simultaneously performed setup operations, which leads to a bottleneck objective function. We formalize this problem and prove that it is NP-hard even when the setup-time matrix satisfies the strong triangle inequality. We also identify an important polynomially solvable special case with unit replacement times and propose an exact greedy algorithm for it.

title: Unlocking seaport flexibility: Coordinated energy-logistics operation for peak and frequency regulation services
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, Shanghai Jiao Tong University (SJTU), Shanghai University of Electric Power, Shanghai Jiao Tong University (SJTU) - Department of Electrical Engineering, Shanghai Jiao Tong University (SJTU) - Department of Electrical Engineering and Tsinghua University - Tsinghua Shenzhen International Graduate School

detail.title: Unlocking seaport flexibility: Coordinated energy-logistics operation for peak and frequency regulation services
detail.abstract: Electrified seaports are increasingly evolving into energy-logistics coupled systems with substantial operational flexibility and emerging potential for ancillary-service provision. This paper proposes a two-stage coordinated scheduling framework for port flexible resources participating in peak-regulation and frequency-regulation services. The framework explicitly couples the vessel-to-yard logistics chain with multi-energy resources, thereby characterizing how logistics operations and energy-resource dispatch jointly reshape the temporal profile of port electricity demand. To support multi-service participation, a unified formulation is developed to coordinate heterogeneous port resources across peak and frequency regulation, with resource-specific flexibility and service-specific delivery mechanisms systematically modeled. A commitment-aligned multi-timescale scheduling scheme is further established by integrating stochastic day-ahead planning with rolling intraday recourse over a shrinking horizon, so that service commitments can be consistently adjusted and delivered under updated operating conditions. Numerical results based on Rizhao Port in China demonstrate that the proposed method reduces operating costs, increases ancillary-service benefits, and enables reliable service delivery with enhanced economic robustness under uncertainty.

title: Collaborative optimization of load migration and energy storage system operation strategy in multiple data centers considering user satisfaction
affiliations: North China Electric Power University, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, North China Electric Power University, affiliation not provided to SSRN and North China Electric Power University

detail.title: Collaborative optimization of load migration and energy storage system operation strategy in multiple data centers considering user satisfaction
detail.abstract: With the rapid development of the global digital economy, the problems of high energy consumption and high carbon emissions in data centers have become increasingly prominent. Building green data centers dominated by renewable energy represents a critical measure to achieve energy conservation and emission reduction. Nevertheless, there exists a severe temporal and spatial mismatch between the computing power demand and renewable energy. By integrating cross regional task migration, multi-energy power supply and operation strategy of energy storage system, a multidimensional collaborative optimal scheduling strategy for computing power and energy collaboration among cross regional multi-data centers is proposed in this paper, while considering regional differences in grid electricity prices, renewable energy output, network bandwidth constraints, and service level agreements. Firstly, modeling key energy equipment and task loads based on six real data centers in the eastern and western regions of China to improve the authenticity of the research; Secondly, an optimization scheduling model targeting the minimization of total cost is constructed; Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed strategy is verified through a case study of cross regional computing power scheduling between eastern and western China. The research results indicate that compared with the independent operation scenario without loads migration, the cross regional collaborative optimization scenario reduces the total cost by 25.9%: by investing 19.8% of the migration cost, the grid electricity purchase cost is reduced by 35.1%, the carbon emission cost is reduced by 10.8%, and the service level agreement penalty cost is completely eliminated. In comparison with the intra-regional collaboration plan, the total cost is decreased by 18.7%, with the grid electricity purchase cost and carbon emission cost reduced by 35.3% and 10.9% respectively. Sensitivity analysis shows that grid electricity prices and renewable energy output are the core driving factors affecting system economy. The proposed operation strategy not only achieves the efficient and low-carbon transformation of data centers and significant economic benefits, but also provides a feasible path for the coordinated development of the digital economy and green energy.

title: Digital patent innovation and corporate international diversification: Evidence from China's emerging market
affiliations: Zhejiang University

detail.title: Digital patent innovation and corporate international diversification: Evidence from China's emerging market
detail.abstract: This study investigates whether and how digital technology innovation drives corporate international diversification—a critical question given that digital technologies are reshaping firm boundaries and global competition, yet empirical evidence on their role in international expansion remains limited. Drawing on panel data from 2,855 Chinese A‑share listed firms between 2005 and 2021 (20,326 firm‑year observations), we employ two‑way fixed effects models, instrumental variable regressions, and counterfactual tests to establish causal relationships. We measure digital innovation using digital patent applications (from the CNRDS database) and international diversification as foreign sales‑to‑total sales ratio (FSTS). Our results show a significant positive association between digital patent activity and international diversification, robust to multiple endogeneity checks. Mechanism analyses reveal that digital innovation facilitates international expansion through four pathways: accelerating firm‑level digital transformation, enhancing information transparency, improving operational efficiency, and easing financing constraints. Cross‑sectional analyses show that these effects are significantly stronger for non‑state‑owned enterprises and firms in traditional industries compared to state‑owned enterprises and digital‑native sectors. These findings suggest that digital innovation helps firms overcome institutional barriers, reduce transaction costs, and reallocate resources for foreign market entry. From a policy perspective, our results imply that fostering digital patent activity and technology diffusion—particularly in traditional industries and non‑SOEs—can enhance international competitiveness in emerging economies. Policies supporting digital infrastructure, intellectual property protection, and technology‑enabled financing mechanisms may amplify these diversification benefits.

title: The Role of Investors in Entrepreneurial Meta-Cognitive Transitions
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: The Role of Investors in Entrepreneurial Meta-Cognitive Transitions
detail.abstract: This study examines how interactions with business angels (BAs) and venture capitalists (VCs) shape entrepreneurs’ metacognitive adaptation processes over time. Drawing on entrepreneurial metacognition and situated cognition perspectives, we investigate how founders monitor, reassess, and reconfigure effectual and causal reasoning heuristics throughout venture financing trajectories. Using a comparative case study of three startups characterized by distinct investment configurations (angel-only, sequential co-investment, and simultaneous co-investment), we show that investor relationships may either constrain or stimulate metacognitive flexibility. Our findings identify three distinct patterns: (i) heuristic homogeneity that reinforces persistence in effectual reasoning, (ii) heterogeneous investor interactions that facilitate progressive transitions from effectuation toward causation, and (iii) entrepreneur-led convergence toward a dominant causal heuristic. By conceptualizing heuristic transitions as temporally unfolding and socially embedded metacognitive processes, this study advances research on entrepreneurial metacognition, effectuation, and investor–entrepreneur relationships under conditions of uncertainty.

title: When Do R&D and CSR Compete? Foreign Market Exposure, Business Groups, and Learning Allocation in Emerging Market Multinationals
affiliations: Washington and Lee University, University of Pretoria - Gordon Institute of Business Science and West Virginia University

detail.title: When Do R&D and CSR Compete? Foreign Market Exposure, Business Groups, and Learning Allocation in Emerging Market Multinationals
detail.abstract: Prior research finds that research and development (R&D) and corporate social responsibility (CSR) are complements in some settings and substitutes in others, with no theory explaining when each prevails. We resolve this puzzle by reframing the two investments as instruments of distinct organizational learning modes, R&D as exploratory learning in unfamiliar technological domains, and CSR as exploitative learning that redeploys accumulated institutional knowledge. For resource-constrained emerging-market multinationals (EMNEs), this reframing transforms the exploration–exploitation trade-off from a structural design challenge into a binding allocation problem, in which firms rationally prioritize the learning mode whose returns dominate in their primary market context. Advanced-market exposure shifts marginal allocation toward exploratory R&D, while emerging-market exposure shifts marginal allocation toward exploitative CSR; dual exposure creates simultaneous learning demands that standalone EMNEs struggle to meet, but that business group affiliates can sustain through a collective learning architecture in which shared R&D platforms, stakeholder networks, and coordinated governance lower the marginal cost of either learning mode. Using panel data on 205 publicly listed Indian manufacturing EMNEs from 2015 to 2024 and a G2SLS estimation strategy with three instruments enabling overidentification testing, we find support for all four hypotheses. The findings reconcile conflicting evidence on the CSR–R&D relationship, extend the ambidexterity literature to resource-constrained contexts, and demonstrate how organizational forms characteristic of emerging markets shape the allocation of innovation-related investments under scarcity.

title: Urban Residents’ Adaptive Expenditure Misaligns with Heat Exposure and Exhibits Spatial Heterogeneity: Evidence from Survey and Spatial Modeling
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Urban Residents’ Adaptive Expenditure Misaligns with Heat Exposure and Exhibits Spatial Heterogeneity: Evidence from Survey and Spatial Modeling
detail.abstract: Economic expenditure incurred by urban residents to alleviate heat-induced discomfort constitutes an important adaptive behavioral feedback to heat risk. Yet how such expenditure relates to heat risk, as well as its heterogeneity across population groups and urban space, remains insufficiently understood. Focusing on the area within Beijing’s Sixth Ring Road, this study analyze the response of urban residents’ subjective adaptive expenditure under high-temperature conditions bying combing 2,025 valid field-based questionnaires with heat exposure risk. Multiple correspondence analysis was used to identify population heterogeneity, and XGBoost was applied to simulate the spatial distribution of subjective adaptive expenditure. The results showed that subjective adaptive expenditure was more strongly associated with subjective risk perception than with objective heat exposure risk. A pronounced mismatch was observed between objective heat exposure risk and subjective adaptive expenditure: every 0.1-unit increase in heat exposure risk was associated with an average monthly decrease of 142.99 CNY, that is USD 20.08 (2024 price, USD 1 ≈ CNY 7.1217), whereas every 1 ℃ increase in the self-reported temperature threshold for adaptive behavior corresponded to an average monthly decrease of 11.70 CNY. With increasing heat exposure, the composition of subjective adaptive expenditure shifted from short-term consumption-oriented spending toward more maintenance-oriented categories. Residents’ heat response patterns display clear clustering characteristics, with age, household registration, and gender emerging as key distinguishing attributes. The total subjective adaptive expenditure of urban residents in Beijing is estimated at approximately 112 million CNY per month, with higher levels in central areas and lower levels toward the periphery. Overall, this study reveals the economic expenditure response characteristics induced by urban residents’ adaptive behaviors under high-temperature conditions, providing quantitative evidence to support differentiated heat risk management and targeted adaptation policies.

title: Long-Run Effects of Early Literacy Policy: Evidence from Mississippi
affiliations: University of Toronto - Department of Economics

detail.title: Long-Run Effects of Early Literacy Policy: Evidence from Mississippi
detail.abstract: Mississippi's remarkable improvement in national fourth-grade reading rankings has generated enormous interest. Prior work documents that the state's 2013 Literacy-Based Promotion Act (LBPA) played a causal role in this rise. This paper examines whether the LBPA affected longer-term outcomes. Using a difference-indifferences approach, I find little evidence that the policy affected ACT scores, the number of students taking the ACT (a proxy for dropout rates given that the exam is mandatory in Mississippi), students' post-secondary plans, or Advanced Placement exam participation and performance. Given these null estimates, I critically reexamine Mississippi's grade 4 test score gains, but continue to find large positive effects. These results suggest that the LBPA's initial impacts were subject to fade-out, highlighting that early literacy policies may need to be paired with sustained investments in later grades to produce lasting improvements.

title: Local Approximation of Systemic Risk in Large Sparse Economic Networks
affiliations: and University of Florida - Department of Industrial and Systems Engineering

detail.title: Local Approximation of Systemic Risk in Large Sparse Economic Networks

declarations.funderStatement: The authors acknowledge support from NSF award No. 2534856.

detail.abstract: Evaluating systemic risk in large sparse economic networks is computationally challenging because equilibrium outcomes depend on the full network structure and the underlying shocks. This paper develops a local approximation framework for risk evaluation based on local weak convergence. We study a class of stable interaction systems on sparse random networks that includes payment-clearing, equity cross-holding, and production-network models arising in financial and supplychain systems. We show that, under local weak convergence of the underlying marked network, the equilibrium outcome at a uniformly sampled node converges in distribution to its local weak limit. We further establish convergence of a broad class of law-invariant risk functionals of the induced loss distribution, including Conditional Value-at-Risk. These results provide an asymptotically justified and computationally scalable surrogate for systemic risk assessment in large sparse economic networks.

title: Collider Bias in Econometrics
affiliations: University of Campinas

detail.title: Collider Bias in Econometrics

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict of interest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This research does not involve human participants, animal subjects, or any data requiring ethical approval. It is a purely theoretical didactic note based on mathematical derivations.
declarations.funderStatement: No funding was received for this research.

detail.abstract: Collider bias arises when conditioning on a common effect creates a spurious association. This note derives, step by step, the asymptotic bias of OLS in a linear model with one collider control. The closed-form result shows how the bias depends on the collider-path parameter, the reduced-form association between X and C, and the error variances, and it explains why the bias vanishes when the collider structure is absent. The derivation is meant as a compact algebraic complement to graphical treatments and as a practical guide for deciding when a covariate should not be controlled.

title: The Economy is Illegible: Rivalry and the Limits of Administrative Knowledge
affiliations: Brock School of Business, Samford University

detail.title: The Economy is Illegible: Rivalry and the Limits of Administrative Knowledge
detail.abstract: Don Lavoie described "rivalry" as "the clash of human purposes." It is unavoidable, and different constellations of laws and norms-institutions-process it differently. They generate different kinds of usable knowledge and, therefore, different patterns of coordination. Competitive coordination processes rivalry through decentralized individual responses to market prices, profits, and losses. Prices, profits, and losses are the stuff of catallactic legibility, which is a pattern of simplified signals emerging from the competitive process that guides discovery. By contrast, administrative coordination processes rivalry through imposed categories and commands, which are the stuff of simplified representations conducive to control, or administrative legibility. The South African Colour Bar is an important instance of the tradeoff between administrative and catallactic legibility.

title: United States: Non-Big Tech Monopolization Litigation
affiliations: Rutgers, The State University of New Jersey - Rutgers Law School

detail.title: United States: Non-Big Tech Monopolization Litigation
detail.abstract: The U.S. government has brought remarkably few monopolization cases in the past several decades. This has changed in recent years with litigation filed against "Big Tech" companies. This piece discusses three recent antitrust cases outside the Big Tech setting, which involve Live Nation/Ticketmaster, John Deere, and Syngenta. The antitrust doctrines of exclusive dealing and tying are central to the cases, with successful outcomes promising to benefit consumers. Courts should carefully consider these longstanding doctrines in industries that are vital to the U.S. economy: farming, live entertainment, and pesticides.

title: When Wording Changes What We Find: The Impact of Inflation Expectations on Spending
affiliations: University of Toulouse 1 - Toulouse School of Economics (TSE), University of Bonn, University Bonn and Deutsche Bundesbank - Research Center

detail.title: When Wording Changes What We Find: The Impact of Inflation Expectations on Spending
detail.abstract: We use a randomized experiment in the Bundesbank Online Panel-Households (n ≈ 3,900) to show that the estimated link between inflation expectations and household consumption flips sign depending on survey wording. This finding reconciles prior contradictory results and has direct implications for central bank survey design. Our experiment systematically varies elicitation framing of consumption question along three dimensions: the reference unit (individual vs. household), the time horizon (past one, 3, or 12 months), and the question type (attitudinal, planned, qualitative and quantitative recall-based). We find that the time horizon and question type significantly influence the estimated relationship between inflation expectations and durable consumption. While the average effect is weak, its sign and magnitude vary strongly with question design. Planned spending and attitudinal questions, such as whether it is a good time to buy, produce very similar negative associations, suggesting that respondents interpret the former as a proxy for future intentions. In contrast, quantitative recall-based questions on past spending yield a modestly positive link, especially for shorter horizons. These results highlight the critical role of survey design in shaping behavioral measurements, offering a novel explanation for mixed findings in the literature and guidance for both research and policy.

title: Code Structure Evolution: When Software Outlives Its Reasons
affiliations: Artificial Intelligence Research Institute (IIIA-CSIC)

detail.title: Code Structure Evolution: When Software Outlives Its Reasons
detail.abstract: Software is not merely a functional artifact; it encodes human knowledge in the form of invariants, architectural constraints, and historically grounded design decisions. As software evolves-through human modification, automated refactoring, or increasingly through generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) code agents-its functionality may be preserved while the epistemic justification embedded in its structure is gradually eroded. This paper develops the concept of Code Structure Evolution (CSE) to analyze this phenomenon. CSE refers to the transformation of structural relations over time and the associated risk of what I call epistemic drift: the degradation of justificatory continuity across structural change, whether or not this degradation is immediately reflected in invariant violation, traceability loss, structural incoherence, or functional failure. The paper defends a general thesis-that epistemic drift is a latent condition of any evolving software artifact-and examines one contemporary case in which this condition becomes acute and empirically visible: legacy-code modification by a GenAI code agent. An illustrative probe suggests that such modifications can preserve functional and structural indicators while leaving substantial justificatory residue unpreserved. I argue that this dissociation reveals a neglected philosophical problem: the nature of software as a repository of justified understanding and the conditions under which that justification can persist across structural change. CSE thus offers a framework for analyzing the epistemic fragility of evolving technical artifacts. GenAI does not create this fragility; it makes it harder to ignore.

title: Inflation Dynamics and Relative PriceDispersion in South Africa: Implications forOptimal Inflation Targeting
affiliations: and University of Pretoria - Department of Economics

detail.title: Inflation Dynamics and Relative PriceDispersion in South Africa: Implications forOptimal Inflation Targeting
detail.abstract: This paper investigates the dynamic relationship between inflation and relative price dispersion (RPD) in South Africa, focusing on the period from 2009 to 2025, a timeframe marked by significant structural changes in inflation targeting. Drawing on both theoretical models—the menu cost and signal extraction frameworks—the study tests their predictions on how inflation influences RPD using a semi-parametric approach. It extends the analysis by employing quantile-on-quantile regression to capture state-dependent effects across the distribution of relative price variability. The South African case is particularly insightful due to its evolving inflation targets, transitioning from a 3-6 percent band (2000) to a 4.5 percent midpoint target (2017), and moving towards a 3 percent target projected for 2025. These policy shifts offer a unique opportunity to explore the nonlinear, U-shaped nature of the inflation-RPD relationship, challenging the traditional view that zero inflation is optimal. Empirically, this study contributes to the scant emerging market literature, complementing prior work but incorporating inflation target changes. The findings have important implications for monetary policy design in emerging economies aiming to lower inflation targets while minimizing distortive effects on price signals and resource allocation.

title: Green Design Studio: A Modular Integration Layer for Cross-Domain Building Performance Simulation
affiliations: Purdue University, Syracuse University, Syracuse University, Syracuse University, Syracuse University,  and Syracuse University - Department of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering

detail.title: Green Design Studio: A Modular Integration Layer for Cross-Domain Building Performance Simulation
detail.abstract: Building performance simulation (BPS) remains underutilized in architectural practice due to three structural barriers: an ontological gap between architectural design representations and simulation engine inputs, redundant model specification across domains, and rigid platform architectures that resist modular extension. This paper presents Green Design Studio (GDS), a cross-domain BPS platform that mitigates these barriers through a two-dimensional modular architecture. Vertically, the platform separates the architect-facing interface, domain-specific translation pipelines, and simulation engine execution into independent layers. The interface layer comprises the Hub, which organizes simulation inputs into six task modules (Space, Enclosure, Service, HVAC, Site, and Advanced) corresponding to progressive design information, and the Refiner, which enables element-level property modification without whole-model authoring. Horizontally, the workflow progresses from a geometric skeleton through staged enrichment to simulation-ready model generation. A Custom Property Database separates architectural design decisions from detailed engineering specifications, exposing modular selections through the user-interface while preserving database-level customizability. The translation pipelines generate EnergyPlus-IDF files for energy simulation and CONTAM-PRJ files for multizone contaminant transport, ensuring geometric and spatial consistency across domains. Additional engines can be incorporated by adding new translation pipelines. The platform is validated against a whole-year end-use energy consumption data for a two-story dormitory with eight apartment units in Syracuse, yielding a monthly Coefficient of Variation of the Root Mean Square Error (CV-RMSE) of 9.2% and a Normalized Mean Bias Error (NMBE) of 3.5%, well within ASHRAE Guideline 14 calibration thresholds. GDS contributes a replicable architecture for extensible, multi-domain, designer-facing building performance simulation.

title: GFNO: A Generalized Fourier Neural Operator Framework for Wind Flow Field Reconstruction from Sparse Observations
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, Wuhan University of Technology, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Hong Kong University of Science & Technology (HKUST)

detail.title: GFNO: A Generalized Fourier Neural Operator Framework for Wind Flow Field Reconstruction from Sparse Observations
detail.abstract: This study proposes the Generalized Fourier Neural Operator (GFNO), a modular framework for reconstructing high-resolution wind fields from sparse sensor observations. GFNO decouples sparse flow reconstruction into an embedding stage that transforms irregular observations into latent grid representations and a Fourier-based operator stage that reconstructs the full flow field.The framework systematically combines four representative embeddings with three Fourier kernels under a unified physics-informed objective. GFNO is evaluated on two complementary datasets, including Dataset I containing 2,000 transient flow snapshots under fixed sensor locations and Dataset II containing 3,360 mean flow fields with varying building layouts, inflow directions under various sensor placements.Results reveal that the optimal embedding strategy depends strongly on dataset characteristics. For Dataset I, multilayer perceptron (MLP) embeddings outperform alternatives because geometric information provides no additional discriminative signal under fixed configurations. In contrast, for Dataset II with varying layouts and sensor placements, graph neural network (GNN) embeddings consistently achieve best performance, highlighting the importance of geometric priors in cross-configuration reconstruction.Across all datasets, U-Net-augmented FNO (U-FNO) consistently delivers best performance, indicating the importance of recovering localized flow structures in sparse reconstruction. Sensor counts from 4 to 32 are systematically investigated, revealing that reconstruction accuracy in Dataset I saturates beyond 16 sensors, whereas GNN-based models in Dataset II maintain near-saturated accuracy with as few as four sensors.Complementary out-of-distribution evaluations assess robustness under unseen inflow conditions and limited training data. The proposed framework provides an efficient data-driven evaluation tool for urban flow reconstruction under complex interference configurations.

title: Taiwan and the Trilemma Tradeoffs
affiliations: Providence College and Roger Williams University

detail.title: Taiwan and the Trilemma Tradeoffs
detail.abstract: Using quarterly data, indices for monetary independence and exchange rate stability are constructed based on Aizenman, Chinn, and Ito (2008). A de facto measure of capital flow openness is calculated based on capital flows. We find that Taiwan’s pursuit of exchange rate stability and increased capital flow openness has led to declining monetary independence in recent years. Furthermore, both exchange rate stability and financial openness could bring low output growth volatility as well as low inflation volatility if foreign reserves can be kept at or above 69% or 74% of nominal GDP, respectively.

title: Discerning Influence: Which Foreign Institutional Investors Shape Environmental Disclosures?
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, University of Queensland - Business School, Indian Institute of Technology Delhi and University of Queensland

detail.title: Discerning Influence: Which Foreign Institutional Investors Shape Environmental Disclosures?
detail.abstract: This study examines the impact of foreign institutional investors (FIIs) on investee firms’ environmental disclosures. In line with prior research, we find that on aggregate the presence of FIIs is generally associated with improved environmental disclosure. However, this effect masks important differences across investor types. Using data from listed firms in India, we examine three environmentally aligned attributes: being a PRI signatory, being an independent investor, and originating from a country with high environmental social norms. If FIIs are classified according to only one of these characteristics, we find a positive effect on disclosure. However, a deeper analysis shows that the impact is largely driven by FIIs with all three attributes. With the exception of the Big Three, FIIs that lack even one of these characteristics do not significantly affect environmental disclosures. Despite holding relatively small ownership stakes, these FIIs appear to exert a disproportionate influence on environmental disclosure practices. Channel analysis shows the effect is due to monitoring rather than these firms selecting companies that already have good environmental disclosures.

title: Inflation Dynamics and Relative PriceDispersion in South Africa: Implications forOptimal Inflation Targeting
affiliations: and University of Pretoria - Department of Economics

detail.title: Inflation Dynamics and Relative PriceDispersion in South Africa: Implications forOptimal Inflation Targeting
detail.abstract: This paper investigates the dynamic relationship between inflation and relative price dispersion (RPD) in South Africa, focusing on the period from 2009 to 2025, a timeframe marked by significant structural changes in inflation targeting. Drawing on both theoretical models—the menu cost and signal extraction frameworks—the study tests their predictions on how inflation influences RPD using a semi-parametric approach. It extends the analysis by employing quantile-on-quantile regression to capture state-dependent effects across the distribution of relative price variability. The South African case is particularly insightful due to its evolving inflation targets, transitioning from a 3-6 percent band (2000) to a 4.5 percent midpoint target (2017), and moving towards a 3 percent target projected for 2025. These policy shifts offer a unique opportunity to explore the nonlinear, U-shaped nature of the inflation-RPD relationship, challenging the traditional view that zero inflation is optimal. Empirically, this study contributes to the scant emerging market literature, complementing prior work but incorporating inflation target changes. The findings have important implications for monetary policy design in emerging economies aiming to lower inflation targets while minimizing distortive effects on price signals and resource allocation.

title: Discretionary Choice, Information Production, and the SUTVA
affiliations: and

detail.title: Discretionary Choice, Information Production, and the SUTVA
detail.abstract: We contrast ex ante information (signal) production and interim effort in open RCTs versus environments where agents choose treatment/control, evaluating/improving RCT transportability. Information production is high under discretion, since signals improve treatment/control choice, raising consumer surplus. Moreover, agents with-signal have added motivation to follow-through with effort to test signal quality. Nevertheless, if signals have sufficiently small effect on consumer surplus, a unique RCT treatment probability recovers population average discretionary treatment effects (ADTE). Here, self-reported treatment preference rates equal observational data rates, a diagnostic. We sign bias and propose RCTs testing/achieving transportability. Preference shocks recover local ADTE.

title: Data Augmentation and EUR Prediction in Tight Gas Fields via MLP-Enhanced GANs
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Data Augmentation and EUR Prediction in Tight Gas Fields via MLP-Enhanced GANs
detail.abstract: With the large-scale development of tight gas in China, accurate prediction of the estimated ultimate recovery (EUR) of tight sandstone gas wells is crucial for evaluating the economic performance of new wells and optimizing development strategies. However, traditional decline curve analysis methods and existing machine learning models typically rely on long-term production data, making rapid prediction difficult immediately after drilling or during early production stages, resulting in significant delays. To address this, we propose MLP-enhanced Generative Adversarial Networks (MLP-GANs), a novel data augmentation framework for EUR prediction using only static geological parameters. By incorporating multilayer perceptrons (MLP) into the GANs architecture, the method effectively generates high-quality synthetic data, substantially expanding the training dataset and improving model generalization and prediction accuracy. The study is based on data from 432 decommissioned gas wells in the central Sulige Gas Field, with MLP and extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) serving as baseline prediction models. When trained on synthetic data generated by MLP-GANs, MLP and XGBoost reduced their mean absolute percentage errors to 6.7% and 6.3%, down from 18.4% and 16.9%, respectively. The results suggest that data augmentation effectively mitigates data scarcity issues and enables reliable EUR forecasting without production data.

title: Machine-Learning Prediction of Cohesion and Internal Friction Angle for Rock Using Bayesian Methods and Meta-Heuristic Optimization
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Machine-Learning Prediction of Cohesion and Internal Friction Angle for Rock Using Bayesian Methods and Meta-Heuristic Optimization
detail.abstract: Based on laboratory-measured physical and mechanical properties of rock materials, this study develops an integrated predictive and analytical framework for shear strength parameters by combining Bayesian methods, machine learning models, and meta-heuristic optimization, with the aim of improving prediction stability and reliability under small-sample conditions. Within a unified data construction and evaluation scheme, the performance characteristics of a Gaussian mixture model (GMM), bidirectional long short-term memory network (Bi-LSTM), Light Gradient Boosting Machine (Light-GBM), and random forest model (RF) are systematically compared for the prediction of cohesion and internal friction angle. By introducing Bayesian inference into different models, parameter uncertainty is explicitly characterized, thereby alleviating the instability of prediction results under small-sample and noisy data conditions. On this basis, multiple meta-heuristic algorithms are further employed to perform global optimization of key hyperparameters in representative models, enabling an investigation of how parameter configurations influence predictive behavior and error distribution characteristics. The results indicate that, under limited experimental data conditions, the Bayesian-based random forest model exhibits relatively superior performance in terms of prediction stability and consistency of error distributions, while meta-heuristic optimization can, to a certain extent, further improve model performance for the given dataset. Overall, the proposed modeling framework can serve as a complementary tool for the analysis and uncertainty assessment of rock shear strength parameters under data-limited conditions, and provides new insights into intelligent modeling strategies and stability evaluation of rock mechanical parameters.

title: Comparison of Basel III-IV and SVWORLD STANDARD 73.5 v1.7 in the Context of Banking Regulation and Financial Sovereignty

detail.title: Comparison of Basel III-IV and SVWORLD STANDARD 73.5 v1.7 in the Context of Banking Regulation and Financial Sovereignty
detail.abstract: This article provides a direct comparison between the international banking regulation standards Basel III-IV and the author's standard SVWORLD STANDARD 73.5 v1.7. For the sake of objectivity and precision, all conclusions are based on the official regulatory documents of the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS). It is argued that the current standards are effective only within a fiat paradigm, treating empty debt obligations as if they were fully fledged assets. It is shown that Sections 18-20 and the mathematical core of SVWORLD 73.5 already implement all instruments for regulating capital, liquidity, and risk, but they are built on the assessment of real economic value rather than nominal value. The standard does not merely replicate Basel; it fully replaces it, being stricter, more transparent, and safer for national sovereignty. Special attention is given to the principle of subordinating traditional microeconomic indicators to a sovereign filter of real backing, as well as to the extension of automatic regulatory mechanisms across the entire financial system.

title: Geopolitical Risk in the Euro Area: Measurement and Transmission
affiliations: Deutsche Bundesbank, Deutsche Bundesbank, Deutsche Bundesbank,  and Deutsche Bundesbank

detail.title: Geopolitical Risk in the Euro Area: Measurement and Transmission
detail.abstract: Geopolitical risk is a major concern for the euro area, yet widely used measures largely reflect a US perspective. We introduce a geopolitical risk indicator tailored to the euro area using local European news sources. Shocks to this index have significant recessionary and inflationary consequences in the euro area, effects that would be missed when relying on the corresponding US-based measure. We estimate that the Russo Ukrainian War imposed substantial output losses and inflationary pressures on the euro area in 2022. Combining structural scenario analysis with end-of-sample now casting, we show that euro area prospects are highly sensitive to future developments in geopolitical risk. We complement these analyses with two news-based measures of sanctions intensity and shortages for the euro area.

title: Environmental Fallout of the U.S.–China Tariff War Across Brazil’s Forest Frontiers
affiliations: Purdue University, University of São Paulo (USP), University of São Paulo (USP), Purdue University, Purdue University, Purdue University, Purdue University and Purdue University

detail.title: Environmental Fallout of the U.S.–China Tariff War Across Brazil’s Forest Frontiers
detail.abstract: The 2018 U.S.–China tariff war sharply restructured global soybean trade, redirecting demand to Brazil after a >70% decline in U.S. exports to China. Using 30-m land-cover data (2002–2024) and causal time-series models, we estimate that soybean expansion contributed to 4.5 million hectares of additional forest loss per year after 2018 across Brazil’s major producing regions. These findings demonstrate how trade-driven supply-chain shifts can undermine forest conservation and sustainability goals, highlighting the need to integrate environmental risk and shock-response mechanisms into global trade governance.

title: From Classroom to Courtroom and Back: Exit, Voice, and the Struggle Over Public Education in America
affiliations: Bar-Ilan University - Faculty of Law

detail.title: From Classroom to Courtroom and Back: Exit, Voice, and the Struggle Over Public Education in America

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None
declarations.funderStatement: None

detail.abstract: In Mahmoud v. Taylor, the Supreme Court recognized for the first time a constitutional right for religious parents to exempt their children from public school instruction, affirming LGBTQ+ identities. This Article argues that Mahmoud inaugurates a troubling new form of “opt-out constitutionalism”: a judicial model that privileges religious exit over civic engagement, transforms exposure to difference into a constitutional injury, and threatens the very foundations of public education in a pluralist democracy. Although framed as a defense of religious freedom, the Court’s decision in Mahmoud ultimately distorts the proper application of strict scrutiny, strays from the core commitments of political liberalism, and undermines the traditional civic mission assigned to public education. By constitutionalizing subjective offense and collapsing the distinction between exposure and coercion, the Court invites an era of fragmented, ideologically siloed education. This Article situates the Court’s turn in Mahmoud within the broader landscape of deepening political polarization and growing civic retreat and turns to comparative constitutional frameworks to identify institutional models that balance religious accommodation with the imperative of democratic integration. Reconstructing the doctrinal landscape, this Article offers a normative and institutional framework for resisting constitutionalized exit and re-centering voice in public education. It argues that preserving the public school as a site of civic encounter, not ideological retreat, is essential to sustaining constitutional democracy in an age of division.

title: Copyright Litigation After Generative AI

detail.title: Copyright Litigation After Generative AI
detail.abstract:
Courts and regulators have increasingly found that AI-generated content is not copyrightable, but that works created with AI assistance may receive protection for the human author’s contribution to or arrangement of AI-generated elements. This Article identifies an unforeseen consequence of this framework: it transforms copyright infringement analysis from a content-based inquiry into a process-based one. Because AI-generated content is often indistinguishable from human-authored material on its face, courts cannot perform the “filtration” analyses that copyright litigation typically requires—separating protectable from unprotectable elements—without investigating the process by which a work was created. Unlike ideas, facts, or other public domain materials, which can be identified from a work’s content, the scope of copyright in an AI-assisted work can be identified only through examination of the prompts, outputs, iterations, and editing decisions that gave rise to the final work. This shift has profound consequences for copyright’s litigation system: early disposition will be all but impossible, discovery costs will balloon, and opportunities for strategic behavior will abound.

 

The Article identifies this problem at its inception and considers solutions that might head it off. Courts might be tempted to abandon rigorous comparison in favor of holistic analysis or an identicalness standard, but both of these approaches would undermine copyright’s policy agenda. Instead, the Article proposes a range of mechanisms that would allow courts to continue using filtration, but make it more administrable: a graduated evidence disclosure requirement in litigation, under which plaintiffs who fail to produce creation records would face a heightened similarity standard; an expanded evidentiary role for the Copyright Office as a repository for AI process documentation; and technological tools that can help verify and refine the evidentiary record. Together, these proposals aim to preserve the most analytically sound form of infringement analysis while adapting its evidentiary demands to the realities of a world of ubiquitous AI-assisted creation.

title: Assessing Synergies, Linkages and the Role of Hainan Special Economic Zone in Development of Natural Rubber Ecosystem
affiliations: Maalexi Inc.

detail.title: Assessing Synergies, Linkages and the Role of Hainan Special Economic Zone in Development of Natural Rubber Ecosystem
detail.abstract:
China has successfully created value and wealth, by integrating its industrial and technological development with Global Value Chains through deployment of economic zones. This paper looks at Hainan Special Economic Zone (‘HSEZ’), which was established as the largest special economic zone in China and has grown into second largest contributor of Natural Rubber (‘NR’) production in China. HSEZ has played a key role in design and development of socio-economic policies by acting as a ‘greenhouse’ to test these policies, and in process delivering extraordinary results. The application of triple helix structure to design policies, utilize institutions and implement initiatives by the HSEZ has allowed it to develop some key clusters within the zone where NR ecosystem is regarded as a great accomplishment. This paper identifies the output variables for socio-economic impact rendered by the HSEZ, and output variables of the local NR ecosystem. It then correlates and regresses them to gain insight on the synergies and linkages between the HSEZ’s vibrant environment and the local NR ecosystem. It also looks into new technologies and innovations that are being diffused from universities and research centers with the help of the private sector, under liberal but protective regulations instituted by the government agencies, and seamlessly flowing into the local NR ecosystem. These innovations are helping to address challenges and transforming this traditional but strategic agricultural industry in China, thereby opening venues for its growth and sustainability. This study builds up on primary data collected from visit to the province, discussions with stakeholders in Hainan and analysis of secondary data from various public sources. The results show that HSEZ, has successfully created a ‘collaborative and conducive environment’ that binds key ingredients of the natural rubber ecosystem together. On one hand, Natural Rubber based entrepreneurial ecosystem has formed significant linkages within the HSEZ thereby influencing its gross regional product, government revenue, employment, investments, trade and innovation. On the other hand, NR based entrepreneurial ecosystem retains its uniqueness, and strengthens its contribution to the global and regional trade supply chains.

title: DSAttNet: Dual Attention-guided CNN with Dempster-Shafer Fusionfor Medical Image Classification
affiliations: Guangzhou University, Guangzhou University, Guangzhou University and Guangzhou University

detail.title: DSAttNet: Dual Attention-guided CNN with Dempster-Shafer Fusionfor Medical Image Classification
detail.abstract: Medical image diagnosis is critical for the early detection of diseases, yet traditional methods are limited by subjective clinical judgment and variability in expertise, often leading to misdiagnosis and inefficiencies. Recent advancements in deep learning have revolutionized medical image analysis, enabling automated and highly accurate diagnostic solutions. This paper proposes DSAttNet, a novel convolutional neural network (CNN) framework that integrates dual attention mechanisms and Dempster-Shafer (D-S) theory for robust medical image classification.DSAttNet combines two independently trained CNNs—ConvNeXt-Base and DenseNet-201,each equipped with dual weight attention modules based on multi-scale convolutions to effectively extract critical features from medical images. The predictions from these base learners are processed using D-S theory with evidence conflict detector and new categories, enhancing the model’s ability to handle uncertainty and improving classification reliability. To evaluate the effectiveness and generalizability of DSAttNet, we conducted experiments on four diverse datasets: Brain Tumor Classification, Skin Cancer Diagnosis (ISIC 2018), Gastrointestinal Disease Classification (Kvasir), and Glaucoma Detection (REFUGE). Experimental results demonstrate that DSAttNet achieves state-of-the-art performance, with accuracy and F1 scores of 82.73% and 77.86% on the Brain Tumor dataset, 84.21% and 73.17% on ISIC 2018, 87.75% and 87.65% on Kvasir, and 92.25% and 72.58% on REFUGE, surpassing many recent models in the literature. Our code is publicly available at https://github.com/LHY-GZHU/DSAttNet.

detail.abstract: In April 2026, the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) resumed deployments of Oracle's Cerner Electronic Health Record (EHR) at Veterans Health Administration (VHA) facilities, continuing a program whose lifecycle cost has escalated from an original $10 billion contract to an estimated $37-$50 billion. This article disputes the three foundational assumptions behind the 2017 decision to replace the VA's VistA with Cerner Millennium via sole-source contract: that VistA relied on obsolete technology, that interoperability with the Military Health System required vendor consolidation, and that VistA modernization was prohibitively costly. Each assumption was flawed at inception and has grown less defensible since. VistA's underlying technology is not obsolete it also powers Epic, the market's dominant EHR; VA and the Department of Defense pioneered standards-based data exchange long before Oracle was contracted; and the cost estimates used to justify the Cerner deal were based on a misreading of the evidence. Critically, two developments have fundamentally changed the modernization calculus: VistA's 130 instances have migrated to a federally certified cloud infrastructure, establishing a modern foundation for enterprise-wide modernization; and the advent of AIassisted coding makes VistA's codebase far more tractable to extend, accelerating timelines and slashing costs-making a decade-long modernization investment of $1-2 billion realistic, against $23-36 billion in remaining Oracle deployment costs. Meanwhile, Oracle deployments have caused patient safety failures, dramatic declines in clinician satisfaction, and persistent disruptions, with 16 of 18 GAO recommendations still unimplemented. Oracle's own nextgeneration EHR signals Millennium's obsolescence, raising questions about long-term support and yet another costly migration. VA should cancel further Oracle rollouts and invest in VistA's proven, modernizable foundation-a fiscally responsible path that better serves veterans, clinicians, and taxpayers. In April 2026, the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) deployed Oracle's Cerner electronic health record (EHR) at four medical centers in Michigan 1-the first wave of thirteen installations planned this year. 2 This is not a simple technical update; it represents a substantial workflow change and an open-ended financial commitment at a resource-constrained department.

title: Health in All Policies in Practice A Competency Framework for Practitioners

detail.title: Health in All Policies in Practice A Competency Framework for Practitioners

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No personal or financial relationships to report.
