keywords: Health in All Policies; HiAP; competency framework; public health workforce; Health Impact Assessment; Cumulative Impact Assessment; environmental justice; community engagement; public health practice; professional certification

detail.abstract:
Health in All Policies has become the dominant North American frame for integrating health and equity into cross-sector decision-making, but its practitioner workforce has never been formally defined. The 2013 Rudolph, Caplan, Ben-Moshe, and Dillon guide established HiAP as a working approach for U.S. state and local government; subsequent research, most recently Suter's 2025 multi-case study, has documented substantial variation in how HiAP is implemented. Implementation has continued through cycles of expansion, defunding, and federal institutional shift. The workforce has sustained the work largely on its own — through professional societies, state and local practice, tribal governments, philanthropic initiatives that come and go, and practitioner networks that survive funding cycles. The competencies distinguishing capable HiAP practice from compliance practice have not been articulated at the level of detail other public-health practice fields take for granted.

This paper offers a practitioner competency framework for HiAP practice. It is organized around seven domains and seven roles, with named competencies at each intersection. The framework addresses the governance and institutionalization work that distinguishes mature HiAP practice from policy advocacy, the implementation maturity progression documented in the Suter 2025 research, and the equity and engagement disciplines anchoring the field's commitment to communities most affected by health inequities. It develops a Lived Experience and Prior Learning Assessment pathway as a route into HiAP practice for practitioners whose preparation comes from organizing, tribal governance, or community-based practice rather than degree programs. The framework is a practitioner reference, not a consensus document, offered to support workforce development across the conditions HiAP work currently faces.

title: Little Impact of ChatGPT Availability on High School Student Test Score Performance
affiliations: Seattle University - Economics & Finance

detail.title: Little Impact of ChatGPT Availability on High School Student Test Score Performance
detail.abstract: In educational settings, AI can be used as a learning aid, but can also be used to avoid schoolwork, thereby passing classes while learning little. Many existing studies on the impact of AI on education focus on AI use in controlled settings or with specialized tools. In this paper, the dropoff in ChatGPT activity during non-school summer months in 2023 and 2024 is used to identify areas with heavy educational AI use and thus estimate the educational impact of AI as it is actually used. I find no meaningful impact of AI usage on high school test score averages in either direction. These results imply that, to the extent that high school students use AI to avoid learning, it either does not matter much for their test performance or is cancelled out by positive uses of AI in the aggregate.

title: Health Impact Assessment in Practice: A Competency Framework for Practitioners

detail.title: Health Impact Assessment in Practice: A Competency Framework for Practitioners

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None.
declarations.funderStatement: None.

detail.abstract:
Health Impact Assessment practice in North America rests on a workforce whose competencies have not been formally defined. Wales is the global reference for HIA workforce development; with the Health Impact Assessment (Wales) Regulations 2025, it becomes the first jurisdiction to require HIA by statute on a meaningful scale. North America operates differently: voluntary practice is the default, the Robert Wood Johnson Foundation–funded Health Impact Project closed in 2018, federal application of Cumulative Impact Assessment is currently paused, and neither statutory infrastructure nor sustained philanthropic foundation underwrites the field. The work has been kept alive by practitioner commitment, by the Society of Practitioners of Health Impact Assessment, by tribal HIA programs, by state environmental justice programs, and by academic training centers. Workforce expectations have not kept pace with actual practice.

This paper offers a practitioner competency framework for HIA in North America. It is organized around seven domains — foundations of HIA and CIA practice, screening and scoping, data and methods, community engagement and power, reporting and recommendations, monitoring and follow-through, and project management and stewardship — and seven roles, including a formal Community Partner / Co-Lead role with named competencies. It treats HIA and Cumulative Impact Assessment as parallel methodologies, addresses industry-commissioned HIA ethics directly, and crosswalks formally to the Wales HIA Support Unit framework. The framework is a practitioner reference, not a consensus document, offered as a contribution to the field's continued development under voluntary practice.

title: Nonlinear Tax Credits and Employment Responses to Wage Shocks: Evidence from the EITC
affiliations: Purdue University

detail.title: Nonlinear Tax Credits and Employment Responses to Wage Shocks: Evidence from the EITC
detail.abstract: The Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC) is widely understood to raise average employment among low-income workers, but less is known about whether its nonlinear schedule changes how employment responds to economic shocks. This paper shows that the answer turns on the earnings-distribution incidence of the shock: the same EITC expansion stabilizes employment responses when eligible workers concentrate in the phase-out region, but destabilizes them when shocks compress wages at the bottom of the distribution and activate phase-in incentives. We introduce a commuting-zone average treatment effect (CZATE) that captures equilibrium labor market responses and exploit three quasi-experimental wage shocks---local economic booms, China import competition, and minimum-wage hikes---that differ in direction and where they strike the earnings distribution. A $100 increase in EITC generosity rotates the wage--employment slope by 0.05--0.20 percentage points per 1% wage change. Stabilization dominates in boom environments where eligible mass concentrates in the phase-out region; destabilization is concentrated among single, low-education women under adverse trade shocks, precisely the group with the densest phase-in exposure. Results are robust to contemporaneous welfare reform and multiple identification checks. The cyclical consequences of EITC expansions depend critically on the schedule position of marginal beneficiaries at the time of the shock.

title: DDUST-Net: Dual deep unfolding sparse transform network for hyperspectral image reconstruction
affiliations: Zhejiang University, Zhejiang University, Zhejiang University, Zhejiang University, Zhejiang University and Zhejiang University

detail.title: DDUST-Net: Dual deep unfolding sparse transform network for hyperspectral image reconstruction
detail.abstract: Compressive spectral imaging enables snapshot acquisition of 3D spectral data cube through coded modulation, but reconstruction from highly compressed 2D measurements remains a severely ill-posed inverse problem. Recently, deep unfolding networks have attracted considerable attention for their interpretability and reconstruction performance. However, most existing methods rely on implicit regularization and cannot explicitly model the structural properties of hyperspectral images. This limits their ability to exploit sparse information in highly aliased measurements and restrains further improvement in reconstruction accuracy. To address this issue, we propose a dual deep unfolding sparse transform network. A sparse transform module and a spectral-wise multi-head self-attention module are integrated into the denoising prior network. In particular, the sparse transform module is unfolded based on learned iterative shrinkage-thresholding algorithm to impose explicit transform-domain sparse constraints, improving local feature extraction. Meanwhile, the self-attention module captures global spectral correlations, enabling effective joint local and nonlocal optimization. Experiments on synthetic datasets show that the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art algorithms in reconstruction accuracy and noise robustness. Results on real data further demonstrate its potential for practical applications.

title: Ethnic Discrimination in the Norwegian Rental Housing Market: Evidence from a Field Experiment
affiliations: Bank of Italy - Research Department, Oslo Metropolitan University, University of Oslo - Ragnar Frisch Centre for Economic Research, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Oslo Metropolitan University

detail.title: Ethnic Discrimination in the Norwegian Rental Housing Market: Evidence from a Field Experiment
detail.abstract: We study ethnic discrimination in the Norwegian rental housing market using a preregistered correspondence experiment with three fictitious male applicants. Two profiles - one with a Norwegian-sounding name and one with an Arabic-sounding name - are both presented as steadily employed warehouse workers, while a third profile with the same Norwegian-sounding name is described as unemployed. Using 2,853 applications submitted on Norway’s main rental platform, we find that the Arabic-named applicant receives substantially fewer positive responses than the otherwise identical Norwegiannamed applicant, with a callback rate close to that of the unemployed Norwegian applicant. Relative to an earlier Norwegian field experiment, the estimated gap does not indicate that discrimination has declined over time. We further show that differential treatment is stronger in tighter and more central rental markets, while it is not systematically related to local anti-immigration voting patterns. These findings suggest that unequal access to rental housing is shaped both by ethnicity and by market conditions that give landlords greater scope to screen applicants.

title: Leak-consistent Linear Cross-Attention for Audio-Visual SpikingNeural Networks
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, Changchun University of Science and Technology, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Leak-consistent Linear Cross-Attention for Audio-Visual SpikingNeural Networks
detail.abstract: Audio-Visual spiking neural networks (AV-SNNs)provide a promising paradigm for energyefficient multimodal perception on resource-constrained edge devices. However, existing AV-SNN fusion methods usually decouple LIF/PLIF-based token generation from subsequent attention feature mapping. As a result,static positive-valued mappings used in kernelized linear attention, such as ReLU or Softplus, cannot explicitly account for the amplitude variations induced by neuronal leakage dynamics, which can lead to scale inconsistency and unstable cross-modal interactions under different temporal configurations. To address this problem, we propose Leak-Consistent Linear Cross-Attention (LC-Linear), a linearcomplexity fusion framework that aligns attention feature mapping with PLIF tokenization dynamics. LC-Linear shares the learnable membrane time constant and the corresponding effective leakage factor from the PLIF tokenization stage, and constructs leakage-aware accumulation proxies for Query and Key features before kernelized attention computation. In addition,a dynamic normalization factor derived from the upper bound of geometric leakage accumulation is introduced to reduce feature scale drift and improve the numerical stability of the linear attention denominator,without adding independent learnable leakage parameters. Experiments on CREMA-D,UrbanSound8K-AV,and MNIST-DVS-NTIDIGITS show that LC-Linear achieves competitive classification performance and improved temporal robustness. On CREMA-D,it obtains 80.04%accuracy,76.4%robust accuracy under controlled temporal perturbations,and a temporal prediction instability of 0.118,demonstrating its effectiveness for stable and efficient audio-visual spiking fusion.

title: ConfSurf: Confidence-Aware Neural Implicit Surface Reconstruction with a Unified Geometric Foundation Model
affiliations: Northeastern University, Northeastern University and Shenyang Aerospace University

detail.title: ConfSurf: Confidence-Aware Neural Implicit Surface Reconstruction with a Unified Geometric Foundation Model
detail.abstract: Neural implicit surface reconstruction increasingly relies on monocular priors to resolve geometric ambiguities. Existing methods suffer from two underexplored limitations. They depend on task-specific estimators with inconsistent outputs, and they apply spatially uniform trust that ignores heterogeneous prior errors. We propose ConfSurf to address both issues. At the prior extraction level, a unified geometric foundation model jointly produces metric depth, camera parameters, and per-pixel confidence in a single forward pass, from which surface normals are further derived. This ensures cross-modal consistency. At the prior fusion level, a single calibrated reliability signal drives adaptive ray selection, reliability-controlled along-ray sampling, and confidence-aware prior supervision. Our framework is agnostic to the foundation model and is instantiated with Depth Anything V3. Experiments on Replica and ScanNet show that ConfSurf reaches F-score@5cm of 93.73\% and 78.25\%, surpassing the strongest prior-guided baseline by 5.68 and 6.45 points. Training takes only 5.2 hours on a single RTX 3090.

title: Adaptive Density-Aware Soft Clustering Federated Learning Framework with Multi-Source Weighted Aggregation and Hypergraph Enhancement
affiliations: Inner Mongolia University of Science and Technology, Inner Mongolia University of Science and Technology and Inner Mongolia University of Science and Technology

detail.title: Adaptive Density-Aware Soft Clustering Federated Learning Framework with Multi-Source Weighted Aggregation and Hypergraph Enhancement
detail.abstract: Clustered Federated Learning (CFL) mitigates data heterogeneity in Federated Learning (FL) by constructing cluster structures among clients. However, hard clustering methods enforce each client to belong exclusively to a single cluster, making it difficult to capture overlapping similarity structures. Although soft clustering enhances structural expressiveness through multi-membership, existing approaches still suffer from fixed threshold dependency, insufficient utilization of aggregation information, and limited collaborative guidance for overlapping clients. These limitations hinder the joint modeling of intra-cluster heterogeneity and inter-cluster structural relationships. To address these issues, we propose an Adaptive Density-Aware Soft Clustering Federated Learning framework with Multi-Source Information Weighted Aggregation and Hypergraph Enhancement (MIWAHGE-SCFL). The proposed framework models soft clustering relationships as a hypergraph and constructs a density-aware client–hyperedge membership matrix by jointly leveraging model parameters and gradient information, enabling fine-grained characterization of overlapping similarities. Building upon this, a two-level optimization mechanism is developed, consisting of hyperedge-level model aggregation and cross-hyperedge collaborative guidance. At the hyperedge level, a multi-source information weighted aggregation method is proposed, which integrates loss evolution trends, predictive entropy-based confidence, and sample size information to improve aggregation stability and robustness. At the cross-hyperedge level, a hypergraph-enhanced model guidance strategy is introduced for overlapping clients, enabling collaborative optimization from both hyperedge models and highly similar models. Extensive experiments on multiple public datasets demonstrate that MIWAHGE-SCFL achieves superior model performance and generalization capability under complex heterogeneous settings.

title: Gendered Pathways and Youth Agency in Sustainable Agriculture Entrepreneurship

detail.title: Gendered Pathways and Youth Agency in Sustainable Agriculture Entrepreneurship
detail.abstract: 1. AbstractEngaging youth in sustainable agricultural entrepreneurship serves as a strategic route for fostering inclusive development in sub-Saharan Africa. Nevertheless, enduring gender inequalities continue to affect participation, access to opportunities, and the recognition of agency. This study explores how young men and women in Zimbabwe's Marondera District navigate the gendered pathways associated with agripreneurship. The study used an integrated Feminist Political Economy and Structuration Theory framework as guiding theories for the research. The study drew on qualitative interviews with 28 youth agripreneurs (14 women and 14 men) from rural and urban settings. Findings reveal patriarchal land tenure systems, exclusionary financial practices, and unequal distributions of unpaid care and agricultural labour as entrenched barriers. These constraints not only limit material access but also affect cognitive, psychological, and aspirational dimensions of entrepreneurship. Despite these challenges, young women demonstrate strong agency. They engage in collective action, leverage digital platforms, innovate in niche markets, and negotiate household and community relationships. Agency is shown to be relational and strategic, exercised within and against structural constraints. The study reframes entrepreneurial success through a capabilities lens, emphasising autonomy, dignity, and social recognition alongside economic outcomes. It contributes to agrarian gender scholarship by illustrating the dynamic interplay between structure and agency. Policy insights highlight the need for gender-transformative youth entrepreneurship ecosystems aligned with Sustainable Development Goals 5 and 8.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Nutrition Management: How Data-Driven Tools Can Improve Diet Planning, Patient Support, and Public Health

detail.title: Artificial Intelligence in Nutrition Management: How Data-Driven Tools Can Improve Diet Planning, Patient Support, and Public Health

declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: Nutrition management has become increasingly complex because of the growth of diet-related diseases, unequal access to professional dietary support, and the rising demand for personalized care in health systems. Artificial intelligence can enhance the support received by patients and communities by transforming fragmented dietary, clinical, behavioral, and population data into more flexible forms of decision support. This paper develops a qualitative conceptual analysis of artificial intelligence in nutrition management through the lens of stakeholder theory. It argues that the value of data-driven nutrition tools depends not only on technical performance, but also on their ability to address the needs of patients, dietitians, clinicians, health services, public health authorities, and affected communities. The paper identifies three main areas of contribution: personalized diet planning, continuous patient engagement, and the integration of nutrition data for public health decision-making. It also examines important weaknesses, including the possible loss of professional judgment, poor or over-standardized dietary advice, algorithmic bias, and weak data governance. The paper argues that artificial intelligence can strengthen nutrition management when it supports human expertise rather than replaces it. Responsible implementation requires culturally responsive design, transparent governance, professional oversight, and diverse models of collaboration.

title: Track-Guided Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning for Autonomous Vehicle Drifting with Minimum-Lap-Time Planning
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, Nanyang Technological University, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Nanyang Technological University

detail.title: Track-Guided Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning for Autonomous Vehicle Drifting with Minimum-Lap-Time Planning
detail.abstract: In Formula 1, drivers optimize racing lines within tire grip limits to minimize lap times; however, in rally racing, drivers intentionally break traction to drift on loose surfaces. This maneuver rapidly aligns the vehicle for corner exits, ultimately reducing lap time. Autonomously executing such maneuvers formulates a complex dual-objective control problem: stabilizing highly nonlinear drift dynamics while strictly minimizing lap time. Addressing this challenge motivates the development of advanced Minimum-Lap-Time (MLT) drift control architectures.This paper proposes a planning-control framework specifically designed for MLT drifting scenario. First, we formulate an optimal control problem to generate a MLT drift planning trajectory, which is used as prior data to train a deep reinforcement learning drift controller. Given that drifting involves extremely large sideslip angles and is therefore challenging to learn directly, a Track-guided Reinforcement Learning (TgRL) drift control method is proposed to enable progressive training in a step-by-step manner—from drift control policy, to drift corner policy, and finally to a comprehensive drift race policy.The reward function incorporates both an instant reward term and an end reward term derived from the Minimum-Lap-Time objective. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework enables the agent to learn a drift racing policy that not only ensures vehicle motion control performance but also effectively reduces lap time.

title: Dynamic Momentum Trading via Deep Q-Networks: An Intelligent Execution Framework for Portfolio Management
affiliations: Hebei Normal University, Hebei Normal University, Toronto Metropolitan University, Hebei Normal University and Toronto Metropolitan University

detail.title: Dynamic Momentum Trading via Deep Q-Networks: An Intelligent Execution Framework for Portfolio Management
detail.abstract: Momentum trading remains one of the most persistent anomalies in financial markets, but its practical implementation faces challenges due to regime shifts, execution uncertainty, and drawdown risk. To address these issues, we propose a Dynamic Momentum Deep Q-Network (DMDQN), an intelligent execution framework that integrates signal extraction, portfolio optimization, and reinforcement learning-based trading decisions. Specifically, DMDQN combines momentum signals with an LSTM-enhanced mean–variance allocation module to construct dynamic portfolios, while a Deep Q-Network is employed to learn optimal execution policies via adaptive rebalancing under changing market conditions. Empirical results from two representative equity markets, China and the United States, show that DMDQN consistently outperforms benchmark strategies, achieving higher average returns and Sharpe ratios with improved drawdown control—performance is further enhanced after incorporating a stop-loss liquidation rule. Ablation studies confirm that each component contributes positively, with the DQN execution module yielding the largest marginal improvement in risk-adjusted performance. Robustness tests across signal types, training protocols, and market environments further demonstrate the strong generalizability of the proposed approach. Moreover, the proposed DMDQN framework effectively reduces the crash risk associated with traditional momentum investing. Overall, DMDQN provides a practical and effective reinforcement learning-based framework for dynamic momentum trading and intelligent portfolio execution.

title: The K-Threshold Volunteer's Dilemma on Networks
affiliations: University of Galway

detail.title: The K-Threshold Volunteer's Dilemma on Networks
detail.abstract: The classical Volunteer's Dilemma (VD) assumes that a single volunteer is sufficient to provide a collective benefit to all participants. However, many real collective-action problems have a threshold structure, i.e., a minimum number of contributors that is required before any benefit is achieved for the members of the group. We study this K-threshold VD on both regular and Erdos-Renyi networks under evolutionary Fermi imitation. We vary the threshold $\kappa$ and record the volunteering rate, the provision probability, and any over-contribution.We report three main findings. Firstly, on $d$-regular graphs the volunteering rate rises monotonically with increasing threshold but the provision probability falls; there is no evidence of a phase transition between K = 1 and K = 2.Secondly, on Erdos-Renyi graphs, at matched mean degree k, the provision is uniformly lower than on regular graphs, but the degree-stratified volunteering rate is essentially flat: under uniform cost, strategies don't vary across degree classes even when payoffs depend on local degree. Thirdly, when the cost is made dependent on the degree, the volunteering rate falls monotonically with increasing cost.

title: Deep Learning and Explainable Artificial Intelligence for Accurate Short-Term Photovoltaic Energy Forecasting​
affiliations: Tekirdag Namik Kemal University, Trakya University and Trakya University

detail.title: Deep Learning and Explainable Artificial Intelligence for Accurate Short-Term Photovoltaic Energy Forecasting​
detail.abstract: This study investigates the predictive performance and interpretability of a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) model in comparison with conventional machine learning approaches, namely Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) and Random Forest (RF), for short-term photovoltaic (PV) energy forecasting. Using a high-resolution time-series dataset comprising 9,854 observations from a single PV system, the study addresses the challenge of accurately modeling highly stochastic solar energy generation while enhancing model transparency. The results demonstrate that LSTM outperforms the benchmark models, achieving the highest accuracy (R² = 0.65, RMSE ≈ 2.00, MAE ≈ 1.04), whereas XGBoost (R² ≈ 0.58) and RF (R² ≈ 0.41) exhibit comparatively lower performance, highlighting the limitations of tree-based methods in capturing temporal dependencies. Model interpretability is examined using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), which identify global solar irradiance and trigonometric temporal features (day_sin, hour_cos) as the dominant drivers of PV output. Furthermore, SHAP interaction analysis reveals a physically consistent relationship between irradiance and temperature, indicating that the positive contribution of solar radiation becomes more pronounced under elevated temperature conditions. The findings demonstrate that integrating deep learning with explainable artificial intelligence provides not only improved predictive accuracy but also enhanced transparency, addressing a critical barrier to the practical deployment of data-driven PV forecasting models.

title: Analysing Moral Bias in Finetuned LLMs through Mechanistic Interpretability
affiliations: University of Bologna, University of Bologna and University of Bologna

detail.title: Analysing Moral Bias in Finetuned LLMs through Mechanistic Interpretability
detail.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have been shown to internalize human-like biases during finetuning, yet the mechanisms by which these biases manifest remain unclear. In this work, we investigated whether the well-known Knobe effect, a moral bias in intentionality judgements, emerges in finetuned LLMs and whether it can be traced back to specific components of the model. We conducted a Layer-Patching analysis across 3 open-weights LLMs and demonstrated that the bias is not only learned during finetuning but also localized in a specific set of layers. Surprisingly, we found that patching activations from the corresponding pretrained model into just a critical layer is sufficient to eliminate the effect. Our findings indicate that social biases in LLMs can be interpreted, localized, and mitigated through targeted interventions, without the need for model retraining.

title: SFAPose: Cross-Species Animal Pose Estimation via Flow-Field Alignment and Species-Aware Text Priors
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, Chengdu University, Guizhou University, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Guizhou University

detail.title: SFAPose: Cross-Species Animal Pose Estimation via Flow-Field Alignment and Species-Aware Text Priors
detail.abstract: To tackle the challenges of semantic ambiguity and cross-scale localization drift stemming from cross-species appearance variations and diverse poses in animal pose estimation, we propose SFAPose, a cross-scale multi-modal fusion network. Specifically, we first introduce the GCSA module into the backbone to effectively suppress noise and enhance key anatomical features via a joint attention mechanism. Subsequently, we propose the KAFAusionNeck, which utilizes a learnable pixel-wise displacement field to perform geometric correction on multi-scale features and achieves precise fusion through keypoint-wise weighting. Finally, we construct the SPALHead to incorporate strong priors at the semantic level, thereby mitigating ambiguities arising from long-tail species and appearance discrepancies. Extensive experiments on the AP-10K and AnimalPose benchmarks demonstrate that SFAPose outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods. Notably, on the AP-10K test set, it improves the baseline AP by 2.2\% and surpasses CLAMP and HRFormer by 1.5\% and 1.8\%, respectively.

title: Virtual Photon Pre-Emission -Part II: Extended Framework for Optical Pumping, Spin Tunneling, and the Magnetic Trigger Test

detail.title: Virtual Photon Pre-Emission -Part II: Extended Framework for Optical Pumping, Spin Tunneling, and the Magnetic Trigger Test
detail.abstract: This paper constitutes Part II of the Virtual Photon Pre-Emission framework, extending the core hypothesis introduced in Part I (Danish, 2025; SSRN: 6751086). Part I established that apparent negative tunneling time in Rubidium BEC experiments arises from the detection of pre-emitted virtual photons transitioning from the force-mediating invisible zone into the detectable visible zone at the medium boundaryrestoring causality without invoking superluminal travel or negative time. The present paper extends this framework in three directions. First, we apply the virtual photon pre-emission model to optical pumping, demonstrating that the dense virtual photon field generated during spin polarization predicts a measurable enhancement of early-arrival signals in pumped versus unpumped BEC samples. Second, we reinterpret spin tunneling as the observable conclusion of a virtual photon field reorganization that precedes the classical spin transitioneliminating the need for instantaneous or superluminal mechanisms. Third, and most critically, we propose three directly falsifiable experiments, culminating in the Magnetic Trigger Test: a novel experimental design in which a pulsed superconducting electromagnetwith no laser source presentshould produce detectable photon signals at the exit boundary of a Rb BEC cloud by driving virtual photons from the invisible to the visible zone. Each proposed experiment generates predictions clearly distinguishable from those of standard quantum optical interpretation. Together, these extensions transform the virtual photon pre-emission hypothesis from a qualitative reinterpretation into a testable, falsifiable physical framework.

detail.abstract: This paper examines the risk-return profile of sustainable equity investment strategies in the euro area in order to assess the presence of a return differential compared to the market index (equity greenium). The equity greenium includes a component related to financial risk (risk premium) and a component associated with investors’ possible preference for ESG themes (preference premium). We find that the returns on sustainable investments diverge from market returns; this result is due to the different exposure to financial risk factors (risk premium), and not to the preference premium. Going forward, the emergence of certain risks not fully priced in and changes in investor preferences could lead to price adjustments and new market equilibria. This suggests the need for close monitoring of the relationship between sustainable investment strategies and the traditional ones.

title: A Solution for Cross-Border and Cross-Currency Interoperability of Instant Payment Systems

detail.title: A Solution for Cross-Border and Cross-Currency Interoperability of Instant Payment Systems

publicationDetails.detailsText: Bank of Italy: Markets, Infrastructures, Payment Systems No. 69
publicationDetails.journalName: Bank of Italy Research Paper Series

detail.abstract:
Instant Payment Systems (IPSs) enable real-time settlement of transactions, providing immediate confirmation of payment status to both parties. However, these systems are predominantly tailored to domestic use and typically operate within specific jurisdictions. Consequently, their capacity to support cross-border and cross-currency transactions is limited.This paper proposes a novel approach for interconnecting IPSs to facilitate cross-border and cross-currency payments, effectively extending these functionalities as an overlay to existing domestic systems. The proposed model introduces a standardized protocol that enables the synchronous processing of instant payments across different IPSs, thereby preserving the immediacy and user experience that are typical of domestic instant payments, even in international contexts. 
Crucially, the proposed interlinking model avoids relying on a centralized hub, which would require designating a central institution to build and manage shared infrastructure. Instead, we advocate using a decentralized approach which, through the adoption of a standardized protocol and the development of an adapter—or gateway—capable of translating and routing messages, allows different IPSs to interoperate directly. This decentralized approach leverages existing bilateral connections between IPSs, repurposing them to form a network of autonomous yet interoperable systems.

detail.abstract: This report presents the payment attitudes of consumers in Italy, based on the ‘Study on the payment attitudes of consumers in the euro area (SPACE) – 2024’, conducted by the European Central Bank between the end of 2023 and the first half of 2024. The main purpose of the report is to provide updated information on the prevailing trends in the use of payment instruments in Italy and, where applicable and relevant, to compare them with those of the euro area and with data from previous surveys (conducted in 2016, 2019 and 2022). The data show that, while cash remains the main payment instrument at the point of sale (POS), especially for low-value purchases (up to €50), its overall usage has gradually declined. Cashless payments are on the rise overall, also owing to an increase in e-commerce purchases. In addition to being the main alternative to cash for POS transactions, cards continue to be the most used payment instrument both in terms of number and value of transactions for online payments. Moreover, mobile payments at the POS and e-payments solutions for online purchases have been growing as well.

title: Model synthesis and identifiability analysis of stiff chemical reaction systems with inVAErt networks
affiliations: University of Notre Dame, Stanford University, University of Notre Dame and University of Notre Dame

detail.title: Model synthesis and identifiability analysis of stiff chemical reaction systems with inVAErt networks
detail.abstract: We consider the problem of learning data-driven replicas for stiff systems of ordinary differential equations arising in chemical kinetics that can be evaluated with high computational efficiency. We first focus on training emulators for families of reaction equations under varying reaction rates, using conditional residual networks or long-short term memory architectures. We then apply a recently proposed data-driven framework known as ``inVAErt networks'' to address the ill-posed inverse problem of inferring reaction rates, integration time, and possibly initial conditions from a target set of species concentrations - a problem that has received relatively little attention in the literature. The proposed approach is demonstrated on chemical systems with reversible and irreversible kinetics, spanning 2 to 20 differential equations, 3 to 20 chemical species, and 3 to 25 reaction rate parameters. Relative root mean squared errors produced by the proposed emulators range from 10^-5 for lower-dimensional systems to 10^-4 and 10^-3 for an air pollution model and a hydrogen-air reaction system, respectively. Manifolds of non-identifiable reaction rates recovered by the proposed approach can be analytically verified for simple systems and are consistent with local identifiability analysis in higher dimensions.

detail.abstract:
Korea is the fastest-aging country in the world. The rapid pace of aging and the increasing
size of the older population pose both challenges and opportunities for Korean society. Coupled
with the rapid technological development driven by digitalization, understanding how older
adults adopt technology has become an important concern for both marketers and policymakers.
This study developed and tested a modified version of the technology acceptance model (TAM)
to explain older adults’ adoption of digital technologies. A comprehensive model that
incorporates senior-specific factors, adoption processes, and outcomes was proposed. A survey
was conducted with 750 Korean seniors aged 60 and older. Results showed that physical health
condition, technology readiness perception, socioeconomic status, and social loneliness
significantly influenced older Korean adults' perceptions of technology and their adoption
process, along with key demographic variables such as age, gender, education, and income. It
was found necessary to add an awareness stage to the adoption process. Seniors’ life satisfaction
was not affected by the adoption process, except for the perceived ease of use of technology.

title: Generative Artificial Intelligence and Startup Innovation in India: Growth Drivers, Investment Dynamics and Sustainability Challenges — An Analytical Study
affiliations: Jai Hind College

detail.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence and Startup Innovation in India: Growth Drivers, Investment Dynamics and Sustainability Challenges — An Analytical Study
detail.abstract: The rapid emergence of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) has transformed global entrepreneurship by reshaping innovation systems, operational efficiency, and digital business scalability. India has emerged as one of the world’s fastest-growing startup ecosystems, with increasing adoption of AI-driven technologies across fintech, healthcare, education, logistics, cybersecurity, retail, and digital services. This study examines the major determinants influencing the growth and sustainability of AI-driven startups in India with particular emphasis on technological innovation, venture capital funding, AI adoption, digital infrastructure, investor confidence, and regulatory frameworks. The research follows a descriptive and analytical design using primary data collected from 150 respondents including entrepreneurs, startup founders, investors, technology professionals, academic researchers, and management students. Statistical tools such as weighted mean analysis, correlation analysis, regression interpretation, and percentage analysis were utilised for data interpretation. The findings reveal that technological innovation, AI adoption, and investor confidence are the strongest drivers of startup growth and scalability. However, regulatory uncertainty, ethical concerns, cybersecurity risks, talent shortages, and excessive dependence on external funding continue to affect long-term sustainability. The study concludes that sustainable AI entrepreneurship in India requires balanced innovation, strong governance mechanisms, ethical implementation, profitability-oriented growth models, and collaborative support from government institutions, investors, industry, and academia.

title: Portrait style classification via multi-perspective representation ensemble learning with metadata fusion
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Portrait style classification via multi-perspective representation ensemble learning with metadata fusion
detail.abstract: Portrait style classification is an important research topic in art data analysis and cultural heritage management. However, most existing approaches rely on encoding an image into a single holistic representation. Portrait paintings, in contrast, contain structurally distinguishable visual regions such as the face, background, and overall composition, and stylistic cues may concentrate in specific regions or emerge through interactions among them. In this study, we propose a multi-perspective representation ensemble learning framework that decomposes each portrait into three visual perspectives and analyzes the contribution of each perspective to style recognition. Each branch refines its features using a branch-specific style encoder designed to reflect regional characteristics, and visual features are integrated with artist and decade metadata at the feature level. To address class imbalance, we adopt the label distribution aware margin loss. Experimental results on a curated subset of WikiArt portraits show that the proposed method achieves an accuracy of 0.8613 and an F1-score of 0.8246, substantially outperforming existing approaches. Furthermore, style-wise quantitative analysis reveals that certain styles rely predominantly on facial cues, whereas others depend more strongly on global composition or contextual information.

title: Uncertainty-Aware Short-Term Photovoltaic PowerForecasting Using XGBoost, LSTM, and AdaptiveConformal Prediction
affiliations: Riphah International University, National University of Sciences and Technology and Riphah International University

detail.title: Uncertainty-Aware Short-Term Photovoltaic PowerForecasting Using XGBoost, LSTM, and AdaptiveConformal Prediction
detail.abstract: The precise short-term forecast of solar photovoltaic (PV) electrical powerplays an essential role in ensuring the stability of the grid and facilitatesthe incorporation of renewable sources of energy into today’s power supplynetwork. Nonetheless, as the levels of solar radiation continue being highlyunstable, traditional deterministic approaches to predicting the power outputfrom PV sources might prove to be ineffective owing to the substantial de-gree of uncertainty involved in such calculations. In this paper, a forecastingmodel is developed considering the issue of uncertainty into accountthrough the use of machine learning and deep learning algorithms alongsideconformal prediction strategies to provide accurate probabilistic predictionsfor the output of solar power. The suggested approach is validated using real-world operation data gathered by DKASC in Alice Springs, Australia, containing 104,291 records obtainedevery five minutes throughout 2024. Forecasting was performed using two models, Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost)model and the LSTM based on predictor values calculated from previous solar radiation and weather information. The conformal prediction was usedfor determining the most suitable intervals for forecasting. According to ex-perimental results, the model based on XGBoost algorithm provides superiorperformance in deterministic form of operation with the average absolute er-ror equal to 7.302 kW, root mean squared error of 16.215 kW, and R-squaredof 0.944, resulting in the normalized mean absolute error of 1.55%. As forthe conformal prediction, its application provided appropriate calibration ofpredictions, resulting in observed coverage rate equal to 93.12% under assumption of 95% probability of coverage and normalized interval width of0.2556. Analysis of inputs reveals that accurate prediction with the help ofonly three time-dependent input variables can be provided by the model. It isworth noting that historical information plays the key role when performingvery short-term solar power forecasting.
