title: A Framework for Integrating Marine Environmental Risk Metrics into Investment Decisions
affiliations: Copenhagen Business School, Copenhagen Business School, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Copenhagen Business School and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: A Framework for Integrating Marine Environmental Risk Metrics into Investment Decisions
detail.abstract: Institutional and corporate investors face increasing regulatory and societal pressure to incorporate biodiversity preservation and ocean sustainability into portfolio decision-making and capital allocation. However, existing environmental, social, and governance (ESG) data and frameworks continue to underrepresent marine ecosystems, limiting their relevance for investment analysis in the ocean sector. Drawing on interdisciplinary scholarship from ocean sciences and sustainable finance for the ocean economy, this paper examines how ESG frameworks can be adapted to better capture marine environmental risks and opportunities. We develop a five-lens framework for integrating ocean sustainability into financial decision-making. The five lenses encompass: (i) the marine materiality exposure lens, which assesses portfolio’s exposure to marine environment-related physical and transition risks and their implications for financial performance; (ii) the ocean sustainability standards lens, which evaluates company adherence to relevant standards and best practices; (iii) the marine pressure attribution lens, which attributes environmental pressures to company operations; (iv) the geolocated marine exposure lens, which identifies the geolocation of activities and their overlap with sensitive marine environments; and (v) the assessment of ocean impact lens that assesses how portfolios mitigate harm to the marine environment while supporting positive outcomes. We emphasize that effective implementation of this framework depends on engaging with the persistent data constraints and ecological complexity that condition the assessment of marine biodiversity. Attention to these challenges is essential if the framework is to support robust financial decision-making, ocean sustainability, and long-term portfolio resilience.

title: When Connectedness Fragments: Inter-Industry Risk Transmission under Geopolitical Stress ​
affiliations: National Taiwan Normal University and University of Strathclyde - Strathclyde Business School

detail.title: When Connectedness Fragments: Inter-Industry Risk Transmission under Geopolitical Stress ​
detail.abstract: This paper examines how geopolitical risk (GPR) is associated with changes in inter-industry risk transmission within the US equity market. Using 17 Fama-French industry portfolios from 1985 to 2025, we show that the relationship between GPR shocks and inter-industry connectedness is nonlinear and state-dependent. GPR shocks are positively associated with connectedness at low-to-moderate quantiles but negatively associated with connectedness at the extreme upper tail. Applying the Bai-Perron structural break framework, we identify nine regimes that broadly coincide with major geopolitical and macro-financial episodes. Focusing on recent regimes in which connectedness declines amid elevated geopolitical stress, directional spillover analysis suggests that fragmentation does not uniformly reduce risk transmission but selectively reallocates it: the Food industry's transmitter role weakens sharply, while the Mines industry becomes more central in the network. Industries with high reshoring/FDI exposure are also associated with a sharper withdrawal from risk-transmitting roles in the most recent fragmentation regime, consistent with supply chain restructuring as a descriptive correlate of market fragmentation.

title: Competitive tension in strategic alliances: Divergent roles of trust and relational intensity in novel value configurations
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and University of Bayreuth

detail.title: Competitive tension in strategic alliances: Divergent roles of trust and relational intensity in novel value configurations
detail.abstract: Strategic alliances often require firms to collaborate with partners that are also actual or perceived competitors. We examine when such competitive tension supports novel value configurations and how this relationship depends on relational governance. Drawing on alliance governance and coopetition research, we conceptualize productive competitive tension as the joint presence of objective market overlap and perceived intra-alliance competition. Using a two-wave dataset of 545 strategic alliances, we find that competitive tension is positively associated with novel value configurations. However, relational governance plays divergent roles: relational intensity strengthens this association, whereas inter-partner trust weakens it. These findings suggest that frequent and substantive interaction helps partners channel competitive tension into value reconfiguration, while high trust may reduce the critical scrutiny, vigilance, and exploratory search required for novelty. The study advances research on strategic alliances and coopetition by showing that relational governance mechanisms are not uniformly beneficial, but differ in how they shape the productive potential of competitive tension. More broadly, the findings highlight the importance of maintaining constructive friction in alliance-based value reconfiguration.

title: Transport Environment Assessment of Aerial Wildfire Suppression Strategies
affiliations: Hanseo University and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Transport Environment Assessment of Aerial Wildfire Suppression Strategies
detail.abstract: This study develops a transport-environment framework for evaluating aerial wildfire suppression as a fleet deployment problem. The model links wildfire spread, mission-cycle operations, base allocation, and suppression strategy under heterogeneous terrain, fuel, weather, and accessibility conditions. The two contrasting cases are evaluated using an integrated effectiveness metric that accounts for burned area, economic damage, carbon emissions, acquisition costs, and operating costs. Results show that efficiency depends on response timing, dispatch geometry, and base accessibility rather than fleet size alone. Earlier access in Palisades enables high effectiveness with a smaller case-optimal fleet, whereas longer access times in Salamis shift the best solution toward larger deployment. The findings support transport-system planning for aerial firefighting under climate-driven wildfire risk.

title: Leading Human-Agent Teams: The ORCHESTRA Framework for Accountable AI Work
affiliations: Suffolk University - Department of Marketing and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Leading Human-Agent Teams: The ORCHESTRA Framework for Accountable AI Work
detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence is moving from a tool that assists individual tasks to an organizational actor that participates in workflows, decision processes, and service delivery. This shift creates a new leadership problem. Managers can no longer focus only on whether employees adopt AI or whether a workflow has been redesigned around AI assistance. They must also learn to orchestrate human-agent teams in which people, AI copilots, software agents, data systems, and governance routines interact continuously. This article develops the ORCHESTRA framework as a practical, research-informed model for leading such systems. Drawing on existing scholarship in employee AI adoption, workflow integration, human-AI collaboration, algorithmic management, sociotechnical systems, automation bias, and responsible AI governance, the framework organizes human-agent leadership into three recurring phases: Design & Enable, Operate & Govern, and Learn & Assure. The framework organizes leadership attention around Objectives, Rules and guardrails, Capabilities, Handoffs, Escalation, Supervision loops, Telemetry, Retrospectives, and Auditability. The article positions ORCHESTRA as an integrative framework developed from academic literature, practitioner dialogue, field-facing AI workflow design artifacts, and applied observation of emerging human-agent work practices. The central argument is that sustainable value from agentic AI will depend less on replacing human judgment than on designing the conditions under which human judgment, machine capability, and organizational accountability can work together.

title: Linking Ecological Thresholds with Hurricane Response: An Operational Eco-DRR Framework for Mangrove Restoration
affiliations: Universidad Nacional de Colombia, National University of Colombia, National University of Colombia, National University of Colombia, Florida State University and National University of Colombia

detail.title: Linking Ecological Thresholds with Hurricane Response: An Operational Eco-DRR Framework for Mangrove Restoration
detail.abstract: Extreme weather events are increasingly disrupting mangrove forests, undermining their structure, function, and the ecosystem services they provide. Although ecosystem-based disaster risk reduction (Eco-DRR) is gaining attention, operational frameworks linking ecological processes with hurricane response remain limited, particularly in tropical island systems. This study develops a decision-oriented Eco-DRR framework that integrates ecological thresholds with hurricane response while incorporating community perspectives. It is applied to the Archipelago of San Andrés, Providencia, and Santa Catalina (Seaflower Biosphere Reserve, Colombian Caribbean), which was severely impacted by Hurricane Iota (Category 4) in 2020. The framework is built on three pillars: ecological restoration principles, adaptation to island conditions, and participatory integration of scientific and local knowledge. It comprises three components: (1) a protocol covering preparedness, response, and restoration phases; (2) a threshold-based decision pathway using indicators such as hydrological connectivity and natural regeneration capacity to determine when passive recovery or active restoration is required; and (3) a cost–benefit layer linking restoration investments to ecosystem service values. Results show that mangrove restoration must be site-specific and process-based, with active interventions justified only when ecological thresholds are exceeded. Community participation is essential for identifying priority areas and aligning actions with locally valued services. Restoration costs range from $3,000 to $1,250,000 per hectare, while ecosystem service values average about $194,000 per hectare annually, indicating strong returns. At the archipelago scale (~210 ha), long-term benefits far outweigh restoration costs. Overall, the framework advances Eco-DRR into a practical, scalable decision-support tool to strengthen resilience in mangrove-dependent socio-ecological systems under increasing climate risk.

title: The Five Harbingers of Organizational Enshittification
affiliations: University of Victoria, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and University of Victoria

detail.title: The Five Harbingers of Organizational Enshittification
detail.abstract: Since the term “enshittification” was coined in 2022, it has achieved viral status and inspired a growing and disparate body of research into its various manifestations. In this paper, we aim to bring structure to this fast-evolving domain of inquiry by providing a clear conceptualization of what we term “organizational enshittification.” We identify five “harbingers” that herald the presence of enshittification in organizations. Two harbingers (Degradation and Extraction) are necessary core mechanisms, where the other three (Lock-In, Secrecy, and Disinformation) can amplify the ability of enshittifying companies to benefit financially, but when implemented in combination with the core mechanisms can lead to increased risks to brands and to corporate reputations. We conclude with guidance on how organizational leaders and employees can detect and fight back against enshittification.

title: How has the COVID-19 pandemic brought opportunities for Industrial Development to peripheral regions? The Case of Yangtze River Delta, China
affiliations: Tongji University, Shandong University, Tongji University and Tongji University

detail.title: How has the COVID-19 pandemic brought opportunities for Industrial Development to peripheral regions? The Case of Yangtze River Delta, China
detail.abstract: Major urban agglomerations serve as the most critical engines for national industrial economic development. Within these regions, the radiation and driving mechanisms from core cities to their peripheries are vital. However, these mechanisms are also susceptible to significant disruption from external shocks. In this paper, we further theorize the relationship between the COVID-19 shock, the linkages between core and peripheral cities, and the industrial dynamics of major urban agglomerations. Taking the Yangtze River Delta as a case study, we employ an intensity-based Difference-in-Differences (DID) approach and draw on business registration and enterprise investment databases to estimate the impact of the pandemic shock on the evolution of local industrial dynamics between 2018 and 2024. Our findings indicate that after the core cities underwent the COVID-19 shock, the path dependence of industrial evolution in their peripheral regions significantly increased. The stronger the economic linkage with Shanghai, the more pronounced this effect. However, as the geographical location of the core and periphery changes, this influence exhibits heterogeneity. This paper examines how three key factors - industrial structure, related variety, and relatedness density with local industries of the peripheral cities in receiving investment inflows from core cities - have shaped the local industrial dynamics after the COVID-19 shock. Our findings have enriched the understanding of the role of the external linkages of heterogeneity in the evolutionary economic geography from the "core-periphery" perspective, regarding the impact on the local industrial evolution, and offer important implications for regional development and adaptive responses in the post-pandemic era.

title: A Secure On/Off-Chain Framework for Malicious Node Detection and Ranking in V2V Energy Trading Using Consortium Blockchain and Beta-Based Trust Model
affiliations: Iran University of Science and Technology, Iran University of Science and Technology and Iran University of Science and Technology

detail.title: A Secure On/Off-Chain Framework for Malicious Node Detection and Ranking in V2V Energy Trading Using Consortium Blockchain and Beta-Based Trust Model
detail.abstract: The escalating adoption of electric vehicles has positioned vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) energy exchange as a vital element of future transportation networks. While recent blockchain-based frameworks have enhanced security and privacy in this domain, they often lack sophisticated mechanisms to detect and mitigate dynamic malicious behaviors from participating nodes. This research addresses this critical gap by introducing a comprehensive, two-layer framework for secure behavioral analysis and malicious node ranking. We enhance a foundational consortium blockchain architecture by integrating a lightweight, dynamic Beta Distribution-based trust model. In our model, intensive computations—such as violation assessment—are executed off-chain by an Assignment Server to mitigate computational overhead and enhance network scalability, while final, immutable trust parameters are recorded on-chain. This hybrid design ensures data transparency while minimizing latency. The framework’s robustness is validated through co-simulations using SUMO and NS-3, confirming high detection accuracy against attacks like On-Off and Bad-mouthing, and demonstrating superior performance in transaction latency and throughput compared to benchmark approaches.

title: Validation of a High-Fidelity Digital Twin for a Low-Voltage Grid Testbed
affiliations: Deutsches Zentrum für Luft und Raumfahrt, Deutsches Zentrum für Luft und Raumfahrt, Deutsches Zentrum für Luft und Raumfahrt, Deutsches Zentrum für Luft und Raumfahrt and German Aerospace Center (DLR)

detail.title: Validation of a High-Fidelity Digital Twin for a Low-Voltage Grid Testbed
detail.abstract: Modern electrical grids are evolving into smart, decentralized systems with high integration of distributed energy resources, bidirectional power flows, and real-time control complexity, motivating the need for virtual modeling frameworks. This paper presents a workflow for building and experimentally validating a high-fidelity digital twin of a laboratory-scale reference grid implemented in real hardware. The grid consists of one 100 kVA supply terminal and six 30 kVA load terminals interfaced through a Speedgoat real-time system and monitored via DEWESoft acquisition tools. The digital twin is implemented in MATLAB/Simulink using fixed-step integration and is iteratively refined. Starting from nominal parameters, the model is calibrated by incorporating measured cable impedances and parasitic capacitance derived from the hardware’s behavior. For validation, five representative load profiles are defined and applied in both the simulated and physical grid environments, including static, dynamic, harmonic, and asymmetric conditions. In addition, a coordinated multi-terminal scenario applies varied profiles simultaneously across all six terminals, further confirming the twin’s robustness. The voltage behavior from the hardware is closely reproduced in simulation, with RMS deviations of less than 0.5 V across all scenarios. The twin’s accuracy is demonstrated across multiple loading scenarios, including asymmetrical and harmonics-rich conditions, where it reliably reproduced per-phase voltage dynamics and neutral current behavior observed in hardware. The results confirm that calibrated digital twins can improve development efficiency and reliability in grid research by reducing physical iteration cycles and enabling safe, repeatable evaluation of grid behavior under complex and dynamic conditions.

title: Neutralising the free-rider effect in energy communities: A comparative analysis of benefit allocation mechanisms for balancing markets
affiliations: Polytechnic University of Valencia, Polytechnic University of Valencia and Polytechnic University of Valencia

detail.title: Neutralising the free-rider effect in energy communities: A comparative analysis of benefit allocation mechanisms for balancing markets
detail.abstract: The integration of battery energy storage systems within renewable energy communities offers a promising avenue to provide grid flexibility through balancing markets. While distributed storage is often financially unviable solely for self-consumption in small-scale residential loads, this study demonstrates that market participation significantly increases community revenues, transforming communal batteries into highly profitable investments. However, participating in bidirectional automatic frequency restoration reserve markets significantly alters local physical energy flows. We reveal that traditional revenue-sharing schemes fail to capture these economic distortions, unintentionally generating a free-rider effect where certain prosumers accrue unearned energy savings while others incur opportunity costs. To address this structural challenge, we develop a mixed-integer linear programming model to simulate an energy community’s participation in automatic frequency restoration reserve markets and conduct a comparative analysis of four benefit allocation mechanisms. We propose a novel ex-post approach, the Net Opportunity Cost Allocation, which utilises a shadow settlement algorithm based on deterministic smart meter data to virtually reconstruct the pure self-consumption baseline. By structurally aligning the physical grid’s impacts with financial market revenues, this method explicitly adjusts each member’s market share to offset any unintended economic gains or losses. The results confirm that this mechanism completely neutralises the free-rider effect, ensuring objective financial neutrality for all participants. Ultimately, this transparent and easily implementable framework increases revenue and profitability for the energy community while ensuring that no user is penalised by market activations, thereby fostering the long-term social trust required to accelerate the widespread deployment of distributed energy resources and storage in energy communities.

title: Long-term building energy load imputation via exogenous-condition-based generative modelling
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, Technische Universitat Berlin, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Technische Universitat Berlin and Technical University Berlin

detail.title: Long-term building energy load imputation via exogenous-condition-based generative modelling
detail.abstract: Reliable energy-load measurements are essential for building energy optimisation, load forecasting, and model predictive control. However, long-term continuous missing load data remain difficult to recover, especially when load sensors are unavailable for extended periods and reliable load observations are absent around the missing interval. Existing machine learning (ML) based imputation methods often rely on recursive prediction or surrounding load values, which can lead to error accumulation and limited applicability under long sensor-outage conditions. To address this limitation, this paper reformulates long-term building energy-load imputation as a non-recursive, weather- and temporal-conditioned generation task. Instead of estimating missing values from previously imputed or neighbouring load measurements, the proposed framework directly generates missing load profiles from the corresponding meteorological and temporal conditions. Long missing periods are divided into independent non-overlapping 24 h segments and represented as multivariate tensors, where weather and temporal variables serve as fully observed contextual channels for reconstructing the missing load channel. Based on this formulation, an enhanced pix2pix-style conditional generative adversarial network (cGAN) is developed with a dilated U-Net generator to capture multi-scale cross-variable dependencies and a PatchGAN discriminator to better recover the realistic local temporal patterns. Experiments across multiple data sources, building types, energy carriers, and seasons show that the proposed method reduces NRMSE by 4.63% to 80.10% compared with selected baselines, demonstrating its potential for long-term building energy-load recovery under practical sensor-outage conditions.

title: An Interpretable Deep Learning Surrogate for Wave Energy Converter Array Design with Predictive Uncertainty Quantification
affiliations: University of Tabriz, University of Sharjah and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: An Interpretable Deep Learning Surrogate for Wave Energy Converter Array Design with Predictive Uncertainty Quantification
detail.abstract: Accurate yet computationally efficient prediction of hydrodynamic interactions in wave energy converter (WEC) arrays remains a major challenge in large‑scale farm design. High‑fidelity solvers provide reliable results but are too expensive for rapid layout exploration, while purely data‑driven surrogates often lack physical consistency and interpretability. This study proposes a hybrid surrogate modeling framework for predicting the array interaction factor (Q‑factor) across diverse wave and geometric conditions. The framework integrates a dual‑branch neural architecture for feature fusion with uncertainty quantification and physics‑based regularization. A physics‑informed neural network (PINN) embeds a pairwise Jensen‑based interaction model into the loss function, constraining downstream device interactions through directional attenuation. This enforces physical consistency while preserving data‑driven flexibility. The model achieves strong performance on unseen data (R² = 0.986, RMSE = 0.0061, MAE = 0.0043). Monte Carlo dropout provides uncertainty estimates with standard deviations mostly below 0.006, and a positive correlation between predictive uncertainty and absolute error (r = 0.334) indicates that the estimates are reliability‑aware. SHAP analysis enhances interpretability by quantifying the influence of geometric spacing and spectral wave parameters. Overall, the framework delivers a fast, physics‑consistent, uncertainty‑aware, and interpretable surrogate model for early‑stage WEC farm layout assessment.

title: Measuring Climate Performance Against National Commitments: A Gap-to-Target Indicator for Kyoto and NDC Cycles
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Measuring Climate Performance Against National Commitments: A Gap-to-Target Indicator for Kyoto and NDC Cycles
detail.abstract: Assessing whether countries effectively implement their climate commitments remains a central challenge under the Paris Agreement. Existing indicators monitor emissions trends, policy effort, or the global ambition gap, but do not provide a harmonised measure of alignment between realised emissions and pledged mitigation targets. This paper introduces a Gap-to-Target indicator that measures the distance between observed greenhouse gas emissions and the emissions levels implied by national commitments under the Kyoto Protocol and successive Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) cycles.The paper develops a transparent and replicable framework to harmonise heterogeneous target formats—including base-year reductions, business-as-usual (BAU) deviations, emissions intensity targets, per capita targets, fixed emissions caps, and conditional commitments—into a common emissions-based metric. The indicator is constructed for a panel of 160 countries over the period 1997--2024, enabling consistent comparisons across countries, income groups, regions, and commitment cycles. In addition to the baseline implementation gap measure, the framework introduces dynamic extensions and an \emph{Adjustment Pace Indicator} assessing whether current emissions trajectories are consistent with the pace required to achieve pledged targets within the remaining time horizon.The results reveal a persistent and widening implementation gap under the Paris framework, particularly during the second NDC cycle despite increased stated ambition. Larger gaps are generally observed among higher-income and more carbon-intensive economies, whereas several lower-income countries remain comparatively closer to target-consistent trajectories. Results remain robust across alternative emissions accounting conventions and BAU specifications.

title: A Method for Refined Industrial Carbon Emission Estimation Based on the Integration of Multi-Source Geospatial Data
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, Wuhan University of Technology, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Wuhan University of Technology, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: A Method for Refined Industrial Carbon Emission Estimation Based on the Integration of Multi-Source Geospatial Data
detail.abstract: Against the backdrop of intensifying global climate change and the advancement of China’s “Dual Carbon” strategy, the industrial sector, as the core energy-consuming sector, plays a key role in China’s low-carbon transition. To address limitations in spatial resolution and sector-level estimation accuracy, this paper proposes a refined method based on multi-source geospatial data. The method integrates nighttime light, electricity consumption, and POI data to construct a composite indicator of industrial activity intensity. A grouped regression model generates industrial carbon emission data in China at 1 km resolution. By applying differentiated weights based on industry carbon emission intensity, emissions for eight major sectors are derived. Results show that model R² ranges from 0.734 to 0.867, and the coefficient of variation remains between 5.5% and 5.6%, indicating good fit and robustness. China’s emissions continue to increase with a slowing growth rate. The spatial pattern shows higher values in the east and lower in the west, with coastal concentration. The emission center remains stable in central and eastern Henan Province. Energy-intensive industries dominate emissions, while technology-intensive sectors such as machinery and electronics are mainly concentrated in developed eastern coastal regions.

title: Unsupervised simulation of incompressible flows with physics‑ and equality‑constrained artificial neural networks
affiliations: University of Pittsburgh and University of Pittsburgh

detail.title: Unsupervised simulation of incompressible flows with physics‑ and equality‑constrained artificial neural networks
detail.abstract: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) have shown considerable promise for solving partial differential equations, yet they have achieved limited success in simulating incompressible flows, particularly at high Reynolds numbers. Existing approaches rely on auxiliary labeled data, supervised pretraining, or reference solutions, and no purely unsupervised method comparable to conventional finite-difference or finite-volume solvers has been demonstrated to date. We attribute this gap to the absence of a robust mechanism for enforcing the divergence-free constraint and boundary conditions to strict tolerances — a capability that is fundamental to the success of conventional incompressible flow solvers. To address this limitation, we adopt the physics- and equality-constrained artificial neural network (PECANN) framework in conjunction with a conditionally adaptive augmented Lagrangian method (CA-ALM), and introduce a pressure-Poisson-based objective function. In the proposed formulation, the residual of the pressure Poisson equation is minimized subject to the momentum and continuity equations and boundary conditions on the primitive variables as equality constraints, with CA-ALM enforcing all constraints to strict tolerances. To enhance robustness for advection-dominated, high-Reynolds-number flows, we further propose an adaptive vanishing entropy viscosity that stabilizes early training without influencing the final predictions. A baseline formulation that omits the pressure Poisson equation and uses the residual of the momentum equations as the objective proves ineffective even with the same constraint-enforcement machinery and network architecture, underscoring the critical role of the proposed pressure-Poisson-based objective function. The method is assessed on several benchmark problems — lid-driven cavity flow at Reynolds numbers up to Re=7,500, three-dimensional unsteady Beltrami flow, and both steady and unsteady flow past a circular cylinder with general inflow–outflow boundary conditions, including an ablation study that identifies admissible conditions on velocity and pressure at the outlet — all without labeled data or supervised pretraining.  Most remarkably, the method captures the spontaneous onset of periodic vortex shedding in unsteady cylinder flow without external perturbations, starting from a randomly initialized network.

title: Industrial Policy, Institutions, and the Growth Multiplier
affiliations: Université de Poitiers

detail.title: Industrial Policy, Institutions, and the Growth Multiplier
detail.abstract: Why do similar industrial policies generate different productivity effects across countries? This paper separates state capacity from market contestability in a Schumpeterian growth model. The resulting compound policy multiplier is increasing in capacity, while its contestability profile is monotonic or inverted-U depending on rent-protection effectiveness. Instrument composition matters: direct R\&D grants raise growth, but untargeted tax incentives operate through a distinct additionality channel. An illustrative calibration yields substantial cross-institutional heterogeneity. Matching the OECD R\&D Tax Incentives Database to UNIDO manufacturing panels (44 countries, 2010--2021), direct grants raise TFP growth significantly more where government effectiveness is strong, while tax incentives show no such interaction—consistent with the additionality literature. The paper provides a structural framework and descriptive evidence, not causal estimates, to guide future quasi-experimental work

title: Ecosystems, DAOs, and Regulations: Preparing for Digital Autonomy

detail.title: Ecosystems, DAOs, and Regulations: Preparing for Digital Autonomy
detail.abstract: The widespread concentration of power in a few large infrastructure providers, and their subsequent abuse of power, has sparked widespread discontent. In the doctoral thesis, various proposals have been investigated to reduce control over infrastructure without hurting their performance. This conclusion of the dissertation answers the question posed in the introduction by integrating the answers provided in the various chapters. First, the observations and conclusions of the chapters are briefly restated. These are integrated and plotted on the IT governance layers. The conclusion proposes Federated Technology Governance (FTG) as a solution for preserving societal benefits but mitigating the centralizing power over technology. FTG is a proposal to restructure the provision of infrastructure. It calls for cooperative ownership over critical infrastructure to both benefit from the scale of technology, but also keep it accountable. The implications for research and public policy are addressed, in particular on digital autonomy and AI.

title: Assertive or Sycophantic? Tone-Task Fit in Human-AI Service Interaction
affiliations: ,  and University of Washington - Michael G. Foster School of Business

detail.title: Assertive or Sycophantic? Tone-Task Fit in Human-AI Service Interaction

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare no conflict of interest.
declarations.funderStatement: No funding was received for this research.

detail.abstract: Sycophancy in LLMs has become a prominent safety and alignment concern, yet its downstream consequences in human-AI interaction remain unclear. In particular, research has not established when a less sycophantic-more assertive tone improves user outcomes and when it backfires, as tone itself is increasingly treated as an engineered feature. We address this gap with a two-stage study. A randomized study identifies a tone-task fit pattern under controlled conditions: assertive tone improves outcomes via perceived authenticity in hedonic tasks, whereas sycophancy improves outcomes in utilitarian tasks through perceived warmth. Second, we extend this test in a customized environment that allows real-time interaction. Findings show that the consequences of assertive versus sycophantic tone are context dependent. This cross-over pattern advances the design of sociotechnically-intelligent AI service agents and reframes tone calibration as a context-sensitive alignment procedure, generating direct implications for preference-based LLM service agent design.

title: Designing IT Governance Beyond Centralized Control

detail.title: Designing IT Governance Beyond Centralized Control
detail.abstract: This paper is the introductory chapter of my dissertation on digital autonomy in inter-organizational information systems. I start by explaining what technology is, and how the application of technology has inherent challenges that need to be faced. In my entire dissertation, I take one of these as my central focus: centralization of power. The article describes the manifold consequences of centralization in digital infrastructure, both positive and negative. There are many proposals to resolve the centralization of power over information technology. Yet these proposals often conflict, or propose wildly different resolutions. This leads to the central question of the entire dissertation. Afterwards follows the setup for the various chapters of the thesis, which have mostly been published elsewhere. I pay particular attention to the field of Information Systems, which is uniquely positioned to help societies, organizations, and individuals regain control over their digital infrastructure.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Cultural Representation in Digital Knowledge Systems: Evidence from Northeast India
affiliations: and

detail.title: Artificial Intelligence and Cultural Representation in Digital Knowledge Systems: Evidence from Northeast India
detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence, particularly large language models, despite the attempts to diversify their usage, may continue to exhibit certain biases in cultural representation. The Northeastern region, with over 200 languages and diverse tribal cultural identities, faces certain under-representation in AI outputs. Recent developments such as Bharat- Gen’s initiative to include Assamese and other Northeastern languages by 2026 may usher in a transformation, however, the limited inclusion of such linguistic diversity in mainstream AI systems may continue to pose several challenges. This study explores the difficulties that such representational disparities may inflict upon the students of non-mainstream regions, particularly Northeast India. A questionnaire was designed drawing upon conceptual discussions of technology acceptance, and examining whether AI outputs are able to provide the actual realities of the region rather than relying on the existing stereotypical knowledge available on mainstream digital platforms. Responses from 120 respondents indicate substantial awareness and conceptual clarity regarding AI, where many students accept using AI for academic convenience; however, there is an increasing confusion regarding whether AI outputs are able to draw upon the existing realities of the region. To extend the analysis beyond descriptive statistics, the study introduces a quantitative analysis using the Artificial Intelligence Perception Index, constructed from Likert-scale responses to get deeper analytical insights. The findings highlight the complex role of AI in academics and raise important questions about technological inclusivity and regional representation within emerging digital knowledge systems. The findings raise broader questions about who these systems are actually built for, and whether regions like Northeast India are being left behind in the process.

title: Lifecycle-Aware Binding of SCIM Resources toDecentralized Identifiers and Verifiable Credentials

detail.title: Lifecycle-Aware Binding of SCIM Resources toDecentralized Identifiers and Verifiable Credentials
detail.abstract: Enterprise identity systems increasingly combine SCIM-based provisioningwith cryptographically verifiable identity mechanisms such as DecentralizedIdentifiers and Verifiable Credentials. These technologies solve different partsof the identity problem. SCIM provides lifecycle governance for accounts,groups, roles, and enterprise entitlements, while Decentralized Identifiers andVerifiable Credentials provide cryptographic control, portable claims, andverifier-side proof validation. In current deployments, these layers are usuallyintegrated through ad hoc workflows rather than a protocol-level binding. Thisseparation creates a security gap: a credential may remain cryptographicallyvalid even after the corresponding SCIM account is deactivated, reassigned,or materially changed.This paper proposes a lifecycle-aware SCIM-DID/VC binding model thatlinks a SCIM resource to a DID subject and associated Verifiable Credentialsthrough a SCIM extension schema, binding proof, credential status reference,and lifecycle-driven revocation behavior. The design does not replace SCIM,DID, or Verifiable Credentials. Instead, it adds a governance layer thatconnects provisioning state with credential validity. We analyze the protocolagainst binding forgery, stale credential use, replay, key-rotation inconsistency,and revocation delay under a defined enterprise threat model. We alsoreport a local prototype evaluation using a Java-based SCIM binding service,an in-memory SCIM resource store, a local DID resolver, and syntheticenterprise provisioning workloads. The prototype shows that the additionalbinding checks introduce modest latency overhead for provisioning workflowswhile providing explicit traceability between account lifecycle changes and credential status updates. The results suggest that lifecycle-aware binding isa practical approach for reducing drift between enterprise identity governanceand verifiable credential ecosystems.

title: The Investment in Financial Technology as Intangible Assets for Firm Value of Financial and Securities Firms in the Securities Exchange of Thailand
affiliations: Mahasarakham University

detail.title: The Investment in Financial Technology as Intangible Assets for Firm Value of Financial and Securities Firms in the Securities Exchange of Thailand
detail.abstract: Abstract: This study examines the effect of the investment in financial technology as the intangible assets value and market value of financial and securities firms in the Securities Exchange of Thailand. The development of intangible assets of Thai financial firms over 2020 to 2024 were generated firstly by utilizing original economic model of Brynjolfsson, et al. (2002) and then, by emphasizing on each type of intangible assets under the conceptual model of Saunders and Brynjolfsson (2016). Next, the modified model is combined with other relevant variables that significantly affect to firm market value based on previous researches. Lastly, the cross-sectional multi-regression procedure was used to find out the relationship between the investment in financial technology as the intangible assets value and firm market value. The findings reveal that the Thai market developed intangible assets as Research and Development (R&D) assets and Brand assets (BA) with significant development during and after COVID-19 outbreak from year 2020 onwards. It also reveals that Net property, plant, and equipment (NPPE), R&D assets (RDA), and Brand assets (BA) are still dominant assets created market valuation in Thai financial firms.

title: TIDRec: Mining Time-Evolving Intent Dynamics from Timestamped Interaction Logs for Data-Intensive Sequential Recommendation
affiliations: Harbin Engineering University, Harbin Engineering University and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: TIDRec: Mining Time-Evolving Intent Dynamics from Timestamped Interaction Logs for Data-Intensive Sequential Recommendation
detail.abstract: Modern information systems increasingly rely on large-scale timestamped user-item interaction logs to support personalized information access in e-commerce, media streaming, online advertising, and other data-intensive environments. In such systems, sequential recommendation is not only a next-item prediction task, but also a data mining and information retrieval problem over structured user-item-time logs. The system must infer the current information need of a user from sparse, noisy, and irregularly spaced behavioral observations and then rank candidate items accordingly. Existing studies have improved sequential recommendation by modeling sequential dependencies, temporal intervals, latent intents, or generative augmentation. In practice, however, interaction logs are often sparse, irregular, noisy, and generated by multiple evolving intents. Static sequence embeddings or static intent prototypes are therefore insufficient for characterizing the user state at the target recommendation time.,To address these limitations, we propose TIDRec, a time-evolving intent dynamics framework for data-intensive sequential recommendation. Instead of treating a user history as a regular item sequence, TIDRec models timestamped interactions as sparse observations of an underlying latent intent dynamics system. Specifically, TIDRec first extracts interaction-level intent evidence from user behavior logs and constructs a Temporal Intent Memory Graph to capture both sequential transitions and semantic associations among non-consecutive behaviors driven by the same intent. A graph neural ordinary differential equation is then used to characterize the continuous-time evolution of intent evidence and infer the target-time dynamic intent state. TIDRec further injects this dynamic intent state into a diffusion-based generative module, thereby guiding recommendation representation generation toward the current information need. To improve robustness under sparse and noisy logs, we design a time-intent consistent contrastive learning objective that preserves stable intent semantics across augmented views at the same target time.,Experiments on four public real-world behavioral datasets show that TIDRec consistently outperforms representative sequential recommendation, contrastive learning, diffusion-based recommendation, continuous-time modeling, and state-space model baselines across multiple top-K metrics under a full-ranking evaluation protocol. Ablation studies, robustness analyses, complexity discussion, and visualization results further demonstrate the effectiveness of time-evolving intent modeling for improving recommendation accuracy, stability, controllability, and robustness in data-intensive personalized information systems.

detail.abstract: This study explored Electrical Technology teachers' enactment of Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge (TPACK) in the teaching of Programmable Logic Controllers (PLCs). Anchored in a qualitative research approach, a case study design was employed to gain rich, contextual insights into classroom practices. The research focused on a population of ten technical high schools offering Electrical Technology (Power Systems) in the Gauteng province, South Africa. A purposive sample of six (6) teachers was selected based on their experience and involvement in teaching Programmable Logic Controllers (PLCs). The data was collected through non-participant classroom observations to capture authentic teaching interactions without interference. Thematic analysis was used to interpret the qualitative data that was primarily described based on what was observed in the classroom, highlighting patterns in how teachers integrate technology with pedagogy and content knowledge. Preliminary findings indicate that, while teachers display fundamental TPACK understanding, its implementation is frequently dependent on available technological resources, confidence in using PLC tools for simulation and curricular alignment. The study anticipates that professional development centred on practical technology integration and TPACK upgrading will be critical in promoting more successful Programmable Logic Controllers' learning. These findings contribute to the wider discussion of integrating Industry 4.0 technology into technical and Vocational Education (VOC).

detail.abstract: This paper presents a direct observational comparison of two wage structures (fixed daily wage and piece-rate) in a small stone crushing unit in rural Rajasthan, India. Under the fixed daily wage system, set at 15% above the statutory minimum, the unit dispatched an average of 13 trucks per day. Following a transition to a piece-rate system, daily dispatch rose to 20 trucks, a 54% increase in throughput with no change to workforce size or machinery. Monthly gross profit increased by approximately 64%, though labour costs rose by 75% and cost per truck by 14%. The paper documents the productivity gains alongside significant drawbacks including machinery degradation, target earning behaviour, and worker income volatility. Drawing on the ILO India Employment Report 2024 and Davis (2021), it argues that wage structures in India's unorganised manufacturing sector are almost never consciously designed, and that this inherited approach systematically suppresses productivity. The findings suggest that incentive alignment through piece-rate compensation can yield substantial output gains in labour-intensive small manufacturing, but introduces safety and maintenance risks that must be actively managed, particularly in operations reliant on unskilled labour.

title: System Dynamics in Supply Chain Management: A Systematic Review of Modeling Roles, Coupling Patterns, and Research Gaps

detail.title: System Dynamics in Supply Chain Management: A Systematic Review of Modeling Roles, Coupling Patterns, and Research Gaps
detail.abstract:
Background. System dynamics (SD) has been applied to supply chain management for over four decades, yet no existing systematic review maps where and how SD has been coupled with structural optimization methods in supply chain network design (SCND) contexts, nor does any review identify which network-decision combinations remain methodologically underserved. Existing reviews are either outdated, domain-narrow, methodologically unsystematic, or exclude the post-2020 disruption literature — a period that generated a significant volume of resilience and hybrid modeling work.

Method. This paper reports a PRISMA 2020-compliant systematic review of peer-reviewed journal articles indexed in Web of Science, Scopus, and EBSCOhost from 1990 to 2025. Three concept clusters — SD method, supply chain domain, and network design decision — delimit the search scope. Each included paper is coded on eight dimensions: network type, decision level, dynamic mechanism, SD model type, coupling pattern, validation approach, industry context, and publication period. Intercoder reliability is assessed on a 15% random sample using Cohen's kappa.

Findings. Preliminary hypotheses posit that SD coupling with structural optimization appears in fewer than 20% of reviewed papers; behavioral validation of SD decision rules is reported in fewer than 30% of papers; and post-2020 work shows increased SD application to resilience without commensurate growth in SD-optimization integration. Battery/EV and pharmaceutical sectors appear structurally underrepresented. A gap map cross-tabulating network type againstdecision level reveals the most acute structural absences: multi-tier and circular network SCND under disruption conditions is rarely addressed by validated, coupled SD-optimization models.

Implications. The review produces a coded dataset that enables quantitative statements about SD's methodological coverage in SCND, a taxonomy of SD modeling roles, a typology of coupling patterns, and a tiered research agenda anchored in documented gaps rather than speculation. The gap map constitutes the primary contribution and is designed to serve as a reference for researchers situating new modeling work.

Italian Abstract: Il lavoro analizza lo sviluppo dell’Open Banking in Italia, concentrando l’attenzione sull’evoluzione dei soggetti autorizzati, le dinamiche competitive e la distribuzione geografica degli operatori. L’indagine, che si avvale di informazioni statistiche raccolte dalla Banca d’Italia a partire dal 2020, combina tecniche descrittive e strumenti quantitativi per offrire una visione dettagliata dei servizi erogati, evidenziando trend, concentrazioni e segmentazioni del mercato. L’Open Banking in Italia, sebbene mostri una crescita significativa, ha ancora un utilizzo marginale, coinvolgendo solo lo 0,13% dei bonifici online e concentrandosi prevalentemente nel segmento B2B, dove le imprese sfruttano l’integrazione con sistemi ERP (Enterprise Resource Planning). Il segmento retail sembra faticare, forse ostacolato dalla concorrenza di strumenti consolidati (carte e digital wallet), da prestazioni tecniche non ottimali e dall’assenza di una proposta di valore chiara per l’utente finale. Un limite degli operatori domestici è rappresentato anche dalla loro scarsa propensione all’internazionalizzazione: solo una minima parte opera oltreconfine, a differenza dei competitor europei.
English Abstract: The study analyses the development of Open Banking in Italy, focusing on the evolution of authorized entities, competitive dynamics, and the geographical distribution of operators. Drawing on statistical data collected by Banca d’Italia since 2020, the research combines descriptive techniques with quantitative tools to provide a detailed overview of the services offered, highlighting market trends, concentration, and segmentation. Although Open Banking in Italy is experiencing significant growth, its adoption remains marginal, accounting for only 0.13% of online credit transfers, mainly concentrated in the B2B segment, where firms leverage integration with ERP (Enterprise Resource Planning) systems. The retail segment appears to be struggling, possibly hindered by competition from established instruments (such as cards and digital wallets), technical limitations, and the lack of a clear value proposition for end users. A further limitation of domestic operators is their low propensity internationalization: only a small share operates across borders, unlike their European competitors.

detail.abstract: This paper examines a central paradox in Bihar's makhana economy: the state contributes roughly 80-85% of global Euryale ferox output, yet primary producers appear to capture only a limited share of downstream value [1, 2]. It develops an evidence architecture for a 2022-2025 district-year framework that links three channels: technological diffusion gaps, intermediation margins, and compliance-related barriers in premium export markets. Using observed 2022 district production rows together with harmonized 2020-2025 trade evidence, the analysis clarifies variable construction, reports data-readiness constraints, motivates testable hypotheses, and sets out an empirical design for later estimation as additional official observations are incorporated [3, 2]. It does not estimate causal effects; instead, it defines the auditable data architecture required for later causal and margin-decomposition work. The paper argues that production dominance alone is unlikely to translate into broad producer gains unless institutional access, processing recovery, and market intermediation are jointly addressed.

detail.abstract: The Indus Delta's collapse constitutes a critical sovereign threat, where the permanent forfeiture of coastal territory to saline intrusion violates Pakistan's territorial integrity and catalyzes internal instability through climate-induced migration. The Jinnah Institute estimates that over 1.2 million people have been displaced from the Indus Delta region in the last two decades, while freshwater flow into the delta has decreased by approximately 80 per cent since the 1950s. Despite chronic failures of surface-water governance, national policy remains largely confined to zero-sum inter-provincial water sharing. This paper argues that the prevailing 'surface-water obsession' reflects a systemic marginalization of the coastal periphery and a significant knowledge gap regarding subterranean hydro-dynamics, treating territorial loss as an unavoidable natural phenomenon rather than a remediable strategic failure. This study employs a policy analysis framework, drawing on peer-reviewed literature, satellite remote sensing data, international climate assessments, and macroeconomic reports to document the divergence between official policy narratives and the geo-chemical reality of land forfeiture. Based on this analysis, the paper concludes that transitioning to decentralized subterranean defense-specifically managed aquifer recharge and composite sluice networks-offers a strategically viable path for a fiscally constrained state. By bypassing negative-sum surface-water politics, this model provides a high-return defense that could preserve the sovereign food basket and reduce economic losses from delta degradation. Ultimately, this strategic pivot secures the vulnerable southern frontier while helping to stabilize internal migration patterns directed toward the already over-congested Karachi metropolitan area.

title: AI-Driven Decision-Support Systems and Entrepreneurial Cognition. A Systematic Literature Review

detail.title: AI-Driven Decision-Support Systems and Entrepreneurial Cognition. A Systematic Literature Review

detail.abstract: Background: The integration of artificial intelligence into entrepreneurial decision-making has accelerated rapidly, yet the cognitive mechanisms through which AI decision-support systems reshape entrepreneurial judgment and strategic reasoning under uncertainty remain theoretically underdeveloped. Existing frameworks address either AI capabilities or entrepreneurial cognition in isolation, leaving their interaction insufficiently integrated across disciplines. Objective: This review systematically examines how AI-driven decision-support systems influence entrepreneurial cognition and strategic decision-making across the venture lifecycle. Method: A systematic literature review of 32 peer-reviewed studies published between 2000 and 2026 (including preprints retrieved up to early 2026) was conducted using Elicit and Semantic Scholar, drawing from entrepreneurship, cognitive psychology, behavioral economics, and human–AI interaction scholarship; thematic synthesis was employed to identify convergent and contested findings. Results: Six cross-cutting themes were identified: automation bias and uncritical AI deference; cognitive augmentation and bounded rationality mitigation; algorithmic bias and epistemic opacity; human–AI complementarity and the structural limits of full autonomy; AI-mediated transformation of opportunity recognition; and trust calibration, explainability, and governance. Synthesizing these themes, this review proposes the AICE Framework (AI-Influenced Cognitive Entrepreneurship Framework), which maps AI decision-support interactions across three venture stages (ideation, launch, and scaling) as a four-column matrix (AI inputs, cognitive processes affected, decision outputs, and risk signals) with a vertical moderating factors bar running across all three venture stages, encompassing AI literacy, entrepreneur experience, and institutional context. Conclusion: AI decision-support systems function as cognitive intermediaries rather than autonomous decision agents, producing augmentation and distortion effects simultaneously depending on individual and contextual moderators. Future research should prioritize longitudinal and experimental designs to trace how sustained AI reliance reshapes entrepreneurial cognition over time.

detail.abstract: International tax environments have become increasingly complex for multinational small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) operating across diverse regulatory and accounting regimes. In this context, financial reporting quality plays a central role in shaping tax governance, compliance consistency, and risk management. This paper develops a conceptual comparative analysis of how accounting choices under IFRS and U.S. GAAP influence tax timing, cash flow predictability, and the credibility of reported tax positions. Focusing on deferred taxes, revenue recognition, foreign currency translation, leasing arrangements, and financial instruments, the study links accounting measurement decisions to tax risk exposure and governance outcomes. Adopting a practitioner-oriented and applied perspective, the analysis demonstrates how high-quality financial reporting functions as a governance mechanism that strengthens compliance, enhances transparency, and reduces regulatory uncertainty in multinational settings. By reframing international tax planning as a governance challenge rather than an optimization problem, the paper contributes to the literature on international accounting and applied tax governance, offering a conceptual framework that is directly actionable for practitioners, regulators, and standard setters operating in multinational environments.

detail.title: Less Engagement, Not Exit: Corporate Venture Capital under U.S. Export Controls
detail.abstract: The U.S. restricts domestic suppliers from exporting advanced technologies to selected Chinese firms through the BIS Entity List. This paper examines the unintended effects of these export controls on corporate venture capital (CVC), exploiting staggered Entity List designations as exogenous policy shocks. While revenue, profitability, and return on assets remain unchanged, affected parent firms reduce new CVC deal activity following the shock without significantly changing total investment amounts. The decline is more pronounced among firms with greater China exposure. Within their pre-existing portfolio relationships, CVC investors become less actively engaged with China-linked startups by reducing lead roles and round size, yet they do not exit these relationships outright, and the China-linked portfolio companies themselves scale back Chinese patent activity post-shock. For new investments made after the shock, affected parents shift toward startups without Chinese patent activity. Overall, export controls reshape both the engagement intensity and the China orientation of CVC-backed entrepreneurial financing.

title: Sprint or Walk? Managing Startup Growth Before Production Capacity Investments
affiliations: , Durham Business School and ESSEC Business School

detail.title: Sprint or Walk? Managing Startup Growth Before Production Capacity Investments
detail.abstract:
Food-tech startups that initially outsource production to contract manufacturers often need to build a sufficiently large base of recurring orders to secure funding for building their own production capacity. However, finding the right speed with which to grow recurring orders requires a delicate balance; growing too fast creates operational challenges and leads to high costs for building the required production capacity, while growing too slowly drains financial resources and may even risk losing the market opportunity. 
To find the right pace of growth, we model a finite-horizon dynamic cost-minimization problem with uncertain sales acquisition, where the startup chooses sales effort in each period to reach a target level of recurring orders. The model incorporates sales effort costs, contract manufacturing costs, and convex capacity-adjustment costs. Reaching the target yields a positive reward. We analyze the structure of the optimal policy. In particular, we derive closed-form solutions for two special cases: deterministic sales acquisition and a single-period model with a two-point distribution of sales acquisition. For the general model, we derive monotonicity properties. We further perform numerical experiments and provide a model extension in which the time window of the market opportunity for the startup is uncertain and can end in every period. 
We find that the optimal growth path balances capacity-adjustment costs with financial losses. When the adjustment costs are more convex, startups should allocate greater sales effort early on. Moreover, because expected losses increase more than proportionally with the target level of recurring orders, founders should carefully assess their operational capabilities before committing to ambitious growth goals. When sales acquisition is uncertain, startups benefit from a more cautious and gradual growth path compared to predictable environments. In contrast, when the timing uncertainty of the market opportunity is high, startups should build sales sooner to secure their market position before the opportunity expires.

detail.title: From "I Created This" to "I Love This": How Interactivity and Diversity Drive Continuance Intention in AIGC Customization
detail.abstract: While Generative AI (AIGC) is increasingly embedded in mass customization, sustaining engagement beyond initial adoption remains a key challenge. Grounded in Self-Determination Theory, this study examines how two AIGC affordances—interactivity and output diversity—translate into continuance intention through perceived design agency and customization satisfaction. We used a sequential mixed-methods design: a survey of 829 users analyzed via PLS-SEM, followed by semi-structured interviews with 13 participants to interpret a key non-significant direct effect. Results show that both affordances positively predict design agency, satisfaction, and continuance intention. However, design agency does not directly increase continuance; instead, satisfaction fully mediates the agency–continuance link, indicating that psychological empowerment must be converted into positively evaluated process and product outcomes to sustain use. Interviews converge with this mechanism, highlighting iterative control, authorship, and outcome evaluation as drivers of retention.

title: Reliability-based Process Optimization of the Surface Roughness of Laser-Cut Structural Steels Using Stochastic Emulators

detail.title: Reliability-based Process Optimization of the Surface Roughness of Laser-Cut Structural Steels Using Stochastic Emulators
detail.abstract: Structural steel components produced by laser cutting must meet prescribed surface-quality limits while remaining economically competitive, yet the strong sensitivity of cut-edge morphology to process parameters makes the identification of cost-optimal operating conditions particularly challenging. In this study, quality of cut-surface is quantified using roughness measurements obtained in the horizontal and vertical directions, together with an area roughness metric.The collected experimental data are used to train data-driven stochastic polynomial chaos expansion models that can reproduce the full stochastic response of these roughness measurements over the selected process domain. The emulators are then embedded within a reliability-based design optimization framework aimed at minimizing the operational cutting cost, while strictly enforcing upper-bound constraints on horizontal, vertical, and area roughness. During the optimization, process feasibility is ensured through a support vector classifier, trained on a dedicated cutting-ability campaign, which excludes parameter combinations associated with defective cuts. The resulting framework enables a reliability-oriented, constraint-driven exploration of the high-dimensional parameter space and identifies economically efficient cutting configurations that satisfy quality of cut surface requirements.

title: Balance-Sheet Effects in the Tail: Large Depreciations and Corporate Investment

detail.title: Balance-Sheet Effects in the Tail: Large Depreciations and Corporate Investment
detail.abstract: How do exchange rate depreciations affect investment when firms borrow in foreign currency? Using a novel panel of 7,136 listed non-financial firms from 27 emerging market economies over 2001–2022, we revisit this question with detailed firm-level data on debt denomination. We merge Compustat Global balance-sheet information with Capital IQ Capital Structure data to construct broad measures of foreign-currency exposure. In linear specifications, we find little evidence that foreign-currency debt systematically depresses investment after a depreciation. The effect emerges, however, in episodes of large depreciations: once exchange rate movements cross high thresholds, firms with greater foreign-currency exposure cut capital expenditures significantly more. This pattern is stronger when China is excluded and is concentrated among non-tradable firms. Our findings suggest that foreign-currency debt is not inherently contractionary, but it becomes a source of vulnerability under extreme currency shocks, helping reconcile mixed results in the literature.

title: Rail Layout Design Optimization for Semiconductor OHT Systems:,A Genetic Algorithm Approach with Simulation-Trained Surrogate Modeling

detail.title: Rail Layout Design Optimization for Semiconductor OHT Systems:,A Genetic Algorithm Approach with Simulation-Trained Surrogate Modeling
detail.abstract: This study addresses the rail layout design problem of overhead hoist transport (OHT) systems in semiconductor manufacturing facilities, focusing on how the placement of turntables and N-branch points affects material handling efficiency and congestion patterns. A genetic algorithm (GA) is employed to systematically explore optimized rail layout configurations, and a machine learning-based surrogate model is developed to replace computationally expensive discrete-event simulation during fitness evaluation. The surrogate model takes structural features of candidate layouts as inputs and predicts six operational performance metrics. Experimental results confirm that WIP- and throughput-related metrics achieve high predictive accuracy, while ACI exhibits lower accuracy due to its dependence on microscopic vehicle interaction dynamics not fully captured by static topology features. The proposed framework provides a practical and scalable tool for rapid evaluation of rail layout alternatives, significantly reducing the design exploration cost in large-scale semiconductor manufacturing facilities.

detail.abstract: ​Failures in industrial automation systems are frequently attributed to mechanical overload; however, hazardous escalation may also originate from latent synchronization-control deficiencies and insufficient operator feedback. This forensic case study investigates a real-world incident in a dual-mandrel de-coiler used in a continuous metal-processing line, where unilateral mandrel withdrawal produced asymmetric coil support and secondary structural damage.A multi-method investigation combining CCTV-based timeline reconstruction, functional control-system verification, geometric field-of-view (FOV) modelling with Monte Carlo uncertainty propagation (n = 10,000), and retrospective NASA-TLX workload profiling was conducted. Timeline analysis revealed that unilateral mandrel disengagement remained undetected for seven minutes despite continuous operator supervision. Post-hoc geometric visibility analysis quantified that 40–60% (mean visible-area fraction 50%; 95% CI [38%, 62%]) of the critical far-side mandrel motion region lay outside the operator’s effective field of view due to equipment geometry and workstation positioning. Functional testing confirmed that compromised synchronization enforcement within the translational control circuit permitted unilateral mandrel motion under nominal inputs.The findings demonstrate how synchronization-control failures and restricted HMI visibility can jointly enable prolonged unsafe conditions. A three-layer vulnerability framework (control enforcement, operator detection capability, and mechanical load integrity) is proposed, together with practical recommendations — independent synchronization alarms, redundant positional feedback, enhanced visual monitoring, and periodic interlock verification — several of which have already been implemented. This study provides industrially derived evidence quantitatively linking HMI constraints with delayed hazard detection in synchronized actuator systems.

title: Infrastructure Meets Intelligence: Combining AMDG Case Infrastructure and Maestro Scenario Protocol for Digital Governance Analysis

detail.title: Infrastructure Meets Intelligence: Combining AMDG Case Infrastructure and Maestro Scenario Protocol for Digital Governance Analysis

detail.abstract: Digital governance research has long struggled to combine the depth of case-based evidence with the comparability required for cumulative inference. Two separate research streams have each addressed half of this problem. The Archer Model of Digital Governance (AMDG) has constructed a reproducible, versioned, 111-case infrastructure in which national reform programmes are made structurally commensurable through a fixed template, five quantitative indices, and deterministic archetype classification. The Maestro protocol has developed a disciplined, structured method for converting that evidence into forward-looking scenario intelligence under conditions of uncertainty. This paper is a methodological-conceptual integration that moves through four analytically distinct stages: a pipeline demonstration through five cross-archetype cases; the inductive emergence of an ARMi-separation hypothesis from the Denmark–Saudi Arabia contrast; retroductive validation of that hypothesis against the top-six ARMi scorers in the full 111-case dataset (Table 5); and proposition refinement grounded in evidence drawn from three regions and two governance archetypes. The paper thus enacts the logic it recommends: moving from method demonstration to evidence-driven theoretical claim through a traceable, reproducible arc. The central empirical finding is that the Digital Skills Maturity Index (DSMI) does not adequately explain governance trajectory when taken in isolation. Saudi Arabia scores 0.944 on DSMI; Denmark scores 0.939. By conventional readiness rankings, the two countries are statistically indistinguishable. Yet their Action Research Maturity Index (ARMi) scores — Saudi Arabia 0.572, Denmark 0.803 — reveal a structural difference in adaptive governance capacity that infrastructure measurement alone cannot detect. Band analysis across the full 111-case dataset confirms that mean ARMi is essentially flat across low-, mid-, and high-DSMI cohorts (0.645, 0.637, and 0.662 respectively), establishing at scale that digital infrastructure investment has no systematic relationship with participatory governance capacity. Retroductive micro-case analysis of the six highest ARMi cases (Norway 0.860, Iceland 0.825, Sweden 0.825, Denmark 0.803, Rwanda 0.794, South Africa 0.791) confirms that high ARMi is achieved through design-stage institutional separation of participatory governance from technology delivery — not through infrastructure investment alone. This finding holds across three regions and two income-level categories, challenging Nordic exceptionalism: Rwanda and South Africa both exceed Finland (0.765) in ARMi through structurally distinct but mechanistically equivalent routes, providing cross-cultural validation of the parallel-programmes principle. The negative evidence from three US Federal programme failures — Medicare (ARMi=0.528, bottom decile), the VA Electronic Health Record Modernisation ($49.8B lifecycle cost, four veteran deaths attributable to delays), and PECOS 2.0 ($200M, nine years, zero functional output) — corroborates the structural account from the opposite direction: absence of institutional separation produces predictable and analytically coherent failure modes. The paper advances four falsifiable propositions for the research agenda, offers a practitioner-facing section of exploratory questions for digital programme commissioners, and argues that case infrastructure and scenario intelligence — integrated as the AMDG+Maestro pipeline — represent, among a small number of studies in digital governance research known to us, a methodological approach that combines reproducible large-N measurement with structured causal scenario analysis. The integrated pipeline produces what neither component produces alone: governance intelligence that is both structurally commensurable and directionally interpretable. The manuscript is published as an SSRN Working Paper; appendices are offered as an online addendum for journal submission.

detail.title: Dynamic Recruitment-based harvest control rules to manage stocks with non-stationary productivity: the Iberian sardine  case study
detail.abstract: Recruitment is a key driver of stock productivity, besides growth and natural mortality, and most stocks experience changes in recruitment productivity linked either to gradual drifts, regime shifts, or sporadic episodes of exceptionally high recruitments (like spasmodic stocks), which challenge the use of static reference points for management. In this work, two adaptative recruitment-based harvest control rules (HCRs) are proposed to manage stocks with non-stationary recruitment productivity: a) the Two Recruitment Levels-based HCR (2RL-HCR), which uses as input the mean probability of occurrence of regular/high recruitments during preceding years; and b) the Multiple Recruitment Levels-based HCR (MRL-HCR), which uses a weighted mean of past recruitment deviations (multipliers) over expectations. The rules were tested on the Iberian sardine stock, which exhibits occasionally high recruitment events and experienced historical changes in productivity. Their performance was compared to the ICES Advisory Rule and the rule currently applied to manage this fishery, using Management Strategy Evaluation throughout different plausible operating recruitment models. The recruitment-based HCRs showed an equivalent or more precautionary performance under poor productivity scenarios, and allowed similar or slightly higher precautionary catches for higher productivity scenarios. The MRL-HCR, in particular, is a fast adaptative advisory-rule, showing robust performance across all operating models without needing any upper catch limit to keep risks of dropping biomass below most putative Blim values lower than 0.05. Their fast and strong adaptability to past changes in recruitment productivity was confirmed through a simulated retrospective application on the sardine fishery. The proposed recruitment-based HCRs align with the dynamic management strategies which adapt harvest to the changes in productivity indicators without requiring understanding the drivers of those changes, like Peterman’s productivity adaptative methods and the dynamic B0 approaches. The main advantage of the recruitment-based HCRs versus ad-hoc elaborated HCRs (which may require years for their formulation, as happened with the currently applied HCR), is that they are generic and easily applicable.  These HCRs are well-suited to recruitment-driven fish stocks (like short-lived or spasmodic stocks), and can accommodate the cycles of benchmarks of most fisheries’ advisory bodies, providing a practical framework for management under non-stationary recruitment dynamics.

title: Low-Latency Stress Testing for AI-Integrated Macro-Financial Risk: An Operator-Splitting Framework with Adaptive Error Calibration and Ontological Safety Controls
