detail.abstract: Modern macro-financial stress testing remains dominated by Monte Carlo simulation, whose latency, often measured in minutes for institutional portfolios, is structurally incompatible with the decision cadence required by large-language-model (LLM) multi-agent workflows. This paper develops a framework that addresses the latency barrier without abandoning institutional accuracy expectations or model-governance constraints in the spirit of Basel III and Federal Reserve SR 11-7. The framework rests on three components. First, a deterministic operator-splitting scheme grounded in the Trotter-Kato product formula decomposes a macro-financial shock surface into domain-specific operators whose joint evolution is reconstructed under a convergence rule. Second, an adaptive error-calibration layer monitors the cumulative splitting error on the fly and recompresses step intensity whenever the observed error approaches an institutionally tolerable terminal bound, enabling latency-accuracy trade-offs to be governed rather than improvised. Third, an ontological routing layer interposed between the numerical core and the LLM consensus layer enforces semantic class boundaries on machine-readable outputs, blocking cross-domain misclassification that would otherwise propagate as hallucination into executive-facing risk narratives. Computational evidence on a working implementation indicates that the deterministic scheme returns terminal-state estimates several orders of magnitude faster than reference Monte Carlo at comparable convergence, on commodity cloud hardware, while the adaptive calibration layer maintains terminal error within the configured institutional bound even under stressed cross-asset regimes. The contribution is methodological. Full implementation details remain proprietary to a working system operated by the author.

title: Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning for Energy Management: A Comparative Evaluation
affiliations: University of Galway and University of Galway

detail.title: Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning for Energy Management: A Comparative Evaluation
detail.abstract: Energy management in distributed energy systems is inherently multi-objective, as practical operation requires balancing economic efficiency, equipment usage, service quality, and operational constraints. Multi-objective reinforcement learning (MORL) is a natural framework for such settings, but its use in energy management remains relatively limited, and systematic comparisons of different MORL algorithms in realistic energy-management environments are still scarce. In this work, we evaluate representative MORL algorithms in two real-data-driven settings: battery scheduling and residential appliance scheduling. The MORL methods are evaluated under both MORL-specific metrics and physical and behavioral metrics that describe actual operating behavior. The results reveal distinct algorithmic tendencies: some methods achieve strong scalarized performance but converge to narrow compromise solutions, while others expose stronger preference sensitivity with different operational consequences across tasks. These findings suggest that MORL-specific metrics, such as expected utility and Pareto-front analysis, are insufficient on their own for selecting MORL algorithms in energy-management tasks and should be interpreted together with physical and behavioral metrics.

title: The Heart, The Head, and The Holy: A Moderated Mediation Model of Boycott-Induced Switching Intention
affiliations: Universitas Pembangunan Nasional Veteran Yogyakarta, Universitas Pembangunan Nasional Veteran Yogyakarta and Universitas Pembangunan Nasional Veteran Yogyakarta

detail.title: The Heart, The Head, and The Holy: A Moderated Mediation Model of Boycott-Induced Switching Intention
detail.abstract: The study investigates the psychological determinants of consumer switching intentions in ideologically motivated boycotts, focusing on how dual-valenced emotional drivers influence the decision to abandon global brands. It examines the mediating roles of attitude, subjective norms, and perceived behavioral control within the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB), as well as the moderating role of religiosity. A total of 355 Indonesian Muslim consumers who actively support boycott movements participated in the survey, and the data were analyzed using PLS-SEM. The findings reveal that both positive and negative emotions significantly shape the TPB cognitive components. Notably, positive emotions such as moral pride and solidarity strongly influence attitudes and enhance perceived behavioral control, challenging the assumption that boycott-induced switching intention is primarily driven by animosity. Religiosity plays a dual role by directly strengthening evaluative and normative beliefs and by significantly weakening the influence of subjective norms on switching intention, indicating a substitution effect between internalized faith and external social pressure. By integrating a dual-pathway emotional structure into the TPB framework, this study advances understanding of how affect and spirituality interact to drive consumer resistance in geopolitical contexts.

title: Who Is Missing From the Model? Algorithmic Invisibility, Governance Gaps, and a Federal Architecture for Veteran Suicide Prevention AI

detail.title: Who Is Missing From the Model? Algorithmic Invisibility, Governance Gaps, and a Federal Architecture for Veteran Suicide Prevention AI

detail.abstract:
In 2023, 6,398 veterans died by suicide. Sixty-one percent were classified by VA as Other Veterans, meaning they had no VHA facility contact in the year of death or the prior year. The Veterans Health Administration's primary suicide prediction tool, Recovery Engagement and Coordination for Health Veterans Enhanced Treatment, draws exclusively from VA electronic health records. Veterans without a VHA facility contact within the model's 24-month scoring window generate no data that the model can use. This exclusion is not random; it reflects the boundaries of the current data architecture.

This paper applies the Lifecycle Equity Framework to examine how REACH VET produces algorithmic invisibility for veterans without recent VHA contact, who account for the majority of veteran suicide deaths, including veterans classified as Other Veterans by VA, National Guard and Reserve members, rural veterans, and those whose only federal contact occurs through crisis lines, emergency care, or community outreach. It documents a governance gap in which outreach programs reach veterans who have not had recent VHA contact but generate no data to update the predictive model, leaving veterans algorithmically invisible the week after a crisis.

Two original governance contributions are proposed. First, a mandatory system-initiated three-point interval mental health contact protocol during inactive reserve status, converting the post-separation period from an unmonitored gap into a structured outreach window. Second, a Universal Risk Signal Repository aggregating post-separation screenings, Veterans Crisis Line contacts, COMPACT Act utilization, and community outreach engagement into a centralized system accessible to VA predictive AI. A legislative pathway involving a Title 10 amendment, explicit congressional authorization, and Privacy Act routine-use expansion is identified as a potential route to statutory authority.

The reviewed comparator nations do not appear to have implemented either mechanism. The governance gap is documented. The architecture is proposed. The legislative pathway is identified.

title: Towards a Strategic Human Factors Digital Twinning Framework for Transport Decarbonisation
affiliations: Heriot Watt University, Heriot-Watt University, Heriot-Watt University, University of Glasgow, Hong Kong Polytechnic University, Heriot-Watt University, Heriot-Watt University and University of Glasgow

detail.title: Towards a Strategic Human Factors Digital Twinning Framework for Transport Decarbonisation
detail.abstract: The TransiT project is pioneering the use of national-scale digital twins for the purpose of rapid decarbonisation of the UK’s transport system. The transport system is designed to service humans, and therefore without adequate representation of human factors in the transport system, any digital twins are likely to be inaccurate. This paper describes a strand of research aiming to approach Human Factors digital twinning from a novel perspective. Instead of starting with computational digital twinning platforms, the approach begins the Abstraction Hierarchy (AH). The AH is then systematically connected to data sources through a novel cyber physical systems audit. This audit provides a bridge to a programmatic solution. The AH combined with the mapping of means-ends links to actual or potential cyber physical information sources. This work points towards a computationally parsimonious yet powerful and strategic Human Factors digital twinning approach. The work provides a framework to describe this approach.

title: Learn-to-Adapt Algorithm: A New Continuous Optimization Method
affiliations: Nanjing University of Science and Technology and Nanjing University of Science and Technology

detail.title: Learn-to-Adapt Algorithm: A New Continuous Optimization Method
detail.abstract: Despite advances in metaheuristic optimization, key challenges remain, including balancing exploration and exploitation, preventing premature convergence, and ensuring robust performance across diverse problem landscapes. This paper presents a novel structured hybrid framework, named Learn-to-Adapt Algorithm (L2A), to deal with these challenges in continuous optimization through two key mechanisms: 1) dynamic ϵ-decay for automated exploration control, gradually shifting focus from global to local search, and 2) gradient-assisted refinement using momentum-driven updates for accelerated convergence. Unlike conventional metaheuristics, L2A’s hybrid approach systematically combines stochastic global sampling with derivative-aware local optimization within a single, cohesive algorithm, demonstrating particular effectiveness in high-dimensional, nonconvex landscapes. L2A’s performance is rigorously assessed against four state-of-the-art metaheuristics (namely CMA-ES, SHADE-ILS, L-SHADE, and jSO), and results demonstrate that it successfully maintains a balance between exploration and exploitation and consistently yields high-quality solutions. The analyzed data and score distribution graphs generated during the evaluation, along with the source code and datasets, are publicly available online [1] at: https://github.com/kashifnjust/L2A.

title: An Interpretable AI-Based Decision-Support System for Adaptive Reservoir Operation under Climate Stress
affiliations: , Nankai University, University of Tabriz, University of Tabriz and University of Tabriz

detail.title: An Interpretable AI-Based Decision-Support System for Adaptive Reservoir Operation under Climate Stress
detail.abstract: Efficient reservoir operation under climate variability requires not only accurate inflow prediction but also intelligent decision-making mechanisms that translate forecasts into adaptive release strategies. This study presents an interpretable AI-based decision-support system that integrates deep learning, hybrid metaheuristic optimization, and system dynamics simulation to improve multi-sector reservoir management under hydrological uncertainty. The proposed framework combines (i) a forecast module based on Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks using multi-source hydro-climatic inputs with cyclical encoding, (ii) an explainability layer employing Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) to quantify predictor contributions, and (iii) a hybrid Genetic Algorithm-Particle Swarm Optimization (GA-PSO) engine for deriving adaptive operating policies. A key contribution lies in the formulation of a demand-adaptive objective function and modified performance indices that enable equitable allocation across competing water-use sectors while capturing both partial and complete shortages. The framework is applied to the Alavian Dam system in Iran under multiple hydrological scenarios, including wet, normal, drought, and severe drought conditions. Results demonstrate that the hybrid optimization consistently reduces shortage magnitudes and vulnerabilities compared to conventional operation policies, while the LSTM model achieves high predictive accuracy across a 12-month forecast horizon (NSE up to 0.90). SHAP analysis further enhances transparency by identifying snow cover, precipitation, and lagged inflows as dominant drivers of inflow variability. By coupling interpretable forecasting with optimization-based decision-making, the proposed system generates adaptive rule curves that improve resilience and sustainability of reservoir operations under climate stress.

detail.abstract:
From independence in 1962 until early March 2020, stakeholders of government primary schools had little to no experience with the use of technology for daily teaching and learning. However, with the coming of the COVID-19 pandemic, there was a sudden radical shift in the educational landscape to prevent the spread of the disease and save lives. Thus, school leadership had to become leaders of virtual schools and provide support for teachers to engage students in this new environment. The purpose of this qualitative study was to determine government primary school principals' leadership practices used to support their teachers to engage in emergency remote teaching during the initial period of lockdown of the COVID-19 pandemic; to discover if there is a relationship between the leadership practices and teachers' perceptions of support, and to investigate the extent to which those leadership practices influenced teachers' perceptions of support to engage in emergency remote teaching. Principals and teachers of government primary schools from one borough in St. George East, Trinidad, completed online surveys, which included demographic data as well as other survey questions about principals' leadership practices used to provide support for teachers in the initial lockdown period of the COVID-19 pandemic, and then a purposive sample participated in interviews.

title: An Improved Projection and Splitting Algorithm for High Dimensional Multi-Objective Combinatorial Optimization: Application to Expert Team Recommendation
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Tsinghua University - Tsinghua Shenzhen International Graduate School

detail.title: An Improved Projection and Splitting Algorithm for High Dimensional Multi-Objective Combinatorial Optimization: Application to Expert Team Recommendation
detail.abstract: Multi-objective combinatorial optimization (MOCO) problems require identifying the complete Pareto front across conflicting objectives, yet exact algorithms based on region partitioning suffer from exponential growth in stored subregions as the number of objectives increases. This paper proposes an improved projection and splitting algorithm that replaces exhaustive region splitting with a bound-updating mechanism. Instead of generating $2^{L-1}$ subregions per iteration, the proposed method produces at most $L$ new subregions, reducing the worst-case space complexity from $\mathcal{O}(2^{(L-2)|Y_N|})$ to $\mathcal{O}(L^{|Y_N|})$, where $L$ is the number of objectives and $|Y_N|$ is the number of non-dominated solutions. Completeness, Pareto optimality, and region uniqueness guarantees are fully preserved. A volume-based region selection strategy is further introduced and proven optimal under mild conditions on the search space. The algorithm is validated on synthetic benchmark instances with $L = 3$ to $7$ objectives and on a real-world expert team recommendation problem using the ca-sandi\_auths co-authorship network. The expert team recommendation problem is formulated as a seven-objective MOCO problem encompassing subject coverage, academic productivity, collaboration potential, innovation index, rank similarity, coauthor ratio, and research balance. Computational results show that the proposed algorithm achieves speedups of $2\times$ to $8\times$ over state-of-the-art exact algorithms and remains tractable at $L = 7$, where competing exact methods time out. A case study demonstrates the practical value of the complete Pareto front for priority-driven team selection and sensitivity analysis.

title: Research on the Prediction Model of Liquid Level in the Closed Paste Filling Goaf Based on the Stacked LSTM-Attention Framework
affiliations: Hebei University of Engineering, Hebei University of Engineering, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Hebei University of Engineering, Hebei University of Engineering, Hebei University of Engineering and Hebei University of Engineering

detail.title: Research on the Prediction Model of Liquid Level in the Closed Paste Filling Goaf Based on the Stacked LSTM-Attention Framework
detail.abstract: Back-support closed paste filling is critical for green and safe coal mining, yet goaf filling level prediction remains challenging due to harsh environments and complex fluid dynamics. This paper proposes a simulation-driven prediction framework using a stacked LSTM-Attention fusion network (DLSTM-Att). First, a Simulink model of the paste filling system is built under 16 working conditions (including pump wear, pipeline blockage, and sensor drift) to generate and augment time-series datasets. Then, a stacked LSTM-Attention model is constructed to learn nonlinear temporal dependencies. Results show the proposed model achieves an R² of 0.89, RMSE of 0.144 m, and MAE of 0.086 m. Compared with single-layer and double-layer LSTM, the RMSE is reduced by 15.8% and 8.3%, respectively, outperforming BiLSTM, CNN-LSTM, and Transformer. Ablation experiments confirm that the stacked LSTM reduces RMSE by 8.2%, and self-attention further decreases RMSE by 4.5% and MAE by 23.2%. The model maintains an R² of 0.86 under 10 dB noise interference and achieves an R² ≥ 0.86 and RMSE ≤ 0.235 m on 4 untrained conditions, meeting industrial accuracy requirements. This work provides an effective solution for intelligent monitoring of paste filling processes.

title: A TWO-PHASE STRATEGY FOR MONITORING DESIGN IN SEWER NETWORKS BASED ON CONTAMINATION BACKTRACKING
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and Kore University of Enna

detail.title: A TWO-PHASE STRATEGY FOR MONITORING DESIGN IN SEWER NETWORKS BASED ON CONTAMINATION BACKTRACKING
detail.abstract: The diffusion of contaminants within sewer networks is a highly complex process. The increasing size and intricate structure of these systems, characterized by numerous potential entry points, make their management particularly challenging. To address this issue, several monitoring strategies have been developed to intercept contamination sources and/or track their spread, thereby supporting intervention priorities.,This work proposes a two-phase strategy for the progressive design of a monitoring system in sewer networks. In the first phase, a depth-first search algorithm is applied to generate a contamination criticality map, namely a ranking of node criticality based on their impact on contaminant diffusion. In the second phase, a tailored topological metric, the Relevance-based In-harmonic centrality, is used to identify the most suitable nodes for sensor placement. The novelty of the approach lies in incorporating information about each node’s capacity to diffuse contaminants throughout the system, defined as the node's criticality, Cn.,The strategy provides a ranking of node importance in the contaminant diffusion process to identify the most suitable nodes for sensor placement, enabling progressive improvement in sensor positioning despite spatial, technical, and economic constraints.,The proposed strategy is presented and validated on a reference sewer system reported in the literature.

title: Routing Heterogeneous Drones with Automated Battery Swapping Machines for Multi-Customer Last-Mile Delivery
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Texas State University and Texas State University

detail.title: Routing Heterogeneous Drones with Automated Battery Swapping Machines for Multi-Customer Last-Mile Delivery
detail.abstract: This study considers the routing problem of a drone-based last-mile delivery network equipped with automated battery swapping machines (ABSMs). In this system, heterogeneous drones are adopted to satisfy customers’ delivery demand, while ABSMs are installed to extend drones’ coverage. Unlike most existing studies that assume a homogeneous fleet and restrict each drone to serving only one or two customers per trip, we allow each drone to serve multiple customers within a single route. We formulate the routing problem as a Mixed Integer Linear Program that minimizes total delivery cost while accounting for payload limits, energy consumption, and battery swapping decisions. To address computational complexity, we develop an efficient branch-and-price algorithm. This study contributes a new modeling and solution approach by explicitly incorporating intermediate ABSM locations as operational decision points within an energy- and capacity-constrained routing setting, and by relaxing conventional ”one-customer-per-trip” assumptions. Numerical experiments demonstrate the scalability of the proposed solution algorithm, and sensitivity analyses illustrate the impact of load capacity and flight range on system performance.

title: Replacing Portland cement can increase concrete’s carbon footprint: a strength-dependent efficiency framework for cementitious binder sustainability
affiliations: Politecnico di Torino, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Politecnico di Torino

detail.title: Replacing Portland cement can increase concrete’s carbon footprint: a strength-dependent efficiency framework for cementitious binder sustainability
detail.abstract: The substitution of ordinary Portland cement (OPC) with supplementary cementitious ma-terials (SCMs) is the dominant industrial strategy for decarbonising concrete construction. Yetcurrent environmental assessments universally quantify the benefit per unit mass of binder, ignoring the higher dosages required to achieve equivalent compressive strength — an overdosage that partially or entirely erodes the apparent carbon advantage. Here we show, through a closed-form dimensionless framework grounded in Abrams’ strength law, that the net carbon efficiency of any cementitious binder is not an intrinsic material property but a function of the target strength class. We introduce three dimensionless descriptors — mechanical efficiency ψα, carbon intensity ψϵ, and water sensitivity ψβ — from which we derive a net efficiency parameter η and an Ashby-type Binder Environmental Performance Plane of Efficiency (BEPPE). A central result is that the geometric structure of the sustainability map is preserved under the extension to binder-specific water sensitivity, which acts as a rescaling of carbon intensity through an effective parameter ψeffϵ = ψϵ ψβ . Applied to GGBS, fly ash, LC3, calcined clays, geopolymers, and the full EN 197-1 blended cement family, the framework reveals that for high-performance concrete (C40/50 and above) several widely adopted SCMs deliver zero or negative net benefit at the mix level. These results establish that sustainable concrete design is a coupled material–process optimisation problem, and call for a revision of current environmental reporting standards for cementitious materials.

title: A Cost-Optimal SPC–Maintenance Framework under Dependent Assignable Causes, Sudden Failures, and Delayed Monitoring
affiliations: University of Qom, University of Qom and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: A Cost-Optimal SPC–Maintenance Framework under Dependent Assignable Causes, Sudden Failures, and Delayed Monitoring
detail.abstract: This research presents a sophisticated integrated framework for Statistical Process Control (SPC) and maintenance optimization within an imperfect production system, addressing the intricate dynamics of Assignable Cause (AC ) dependencies, sudden equipment failures, and delayed monitoring strategies. The model delineates ten distinct scenarios to encapsulate process deviations, failures, and maintenance interventions, utilizing Weibull distributions to characterize failure time behaviors. A robust cost structure is formulated, encompassing quality loss, sampling, false alarm, and maintenance costs, with the objective of minimizing the total expected cost per unit time while satisfying stringent operational constraints. Given the non-convex and computationally intensive nature of the optimization problem, the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm is employed to derive optimal decision variables, including sample size, sampling interval, and control chart limits. Numerical evaluations, conducted using a Taguchi L12 orthogonal array, demonstrate the model’s superior performance, achieving average cost reductions of 22.12% when incorporating AC dependencies, 11.01% with sudden failure considerations, and 4.17% with delayed monitoring, compared to simplified baseline models. These findings underscore the model’s robustness and practical utility for high-reliability industries, such as automotive, electronics, and pharmaceuticals, where process stability and cost efficiency are paramount. The proposed framework provides a solid foundation for developing advanced, cost-effective SPC and maintenance strategies, with future research avenues including the exploration of alternative failure distributions, integration of real-time IoT sensor data, and extension to multi-stage production systems.

title: Extension-layer fine-tuning for transfer learning in multi-agent reinforcement learning-based HVAC control​
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Huazhong University of Science and Technology - School of Environmental Science & Engineering and Hunan University - College of Civil Engineering

detail.title: Extension-layer fine-tuning for transfer learning in multi-agent reinforcement learning-based HVAC control​
detail.abstract: Reinforcement learning  has shown strong potential for heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) control, but its practical application is limited by high training costs and insufficient cross-environment generalization. Although existing transfer learning methods can partly alleviate this issue, their transfer stability and adaptability remain limited in complex HVAC systems involving multi-agent interactions. To address this challenge, this study develops an extension-layer fine-tuning strategy within the multi-agent deep deterministic policy gradient (MADDPG) framework for transferring multifunctional HVAC control policies, where separate agents regulate indoor temperature setpoints and fresh-air ventilation. During transfer, the pretrained actor and critic networks are retained as transferable knowledge backbones, and newly added adaptation layers are trained to capture target-environment-specific policy and value-function representations. The proposed strategy is compared with partial fine-tuning, full-model fine-tuning, MADDPG trained from scratch, and a rule-based controller under cross-climate and cross-building-type transfer scenarios. The results show that, across all test scenarios, the proposed strategy maintains indoor temperature and CO2 concentration within prescribed ranges while achieving energy-saving performance comparable to fully trained MADDPG. In addition, compared with training from scratch, transfer learning reduces retraining time by more than 90%, and the additional computational burden introduced by the newly added adaptation layers is limited. These results indicate that extension-layer fine-tuning provides an effective pathway for efficiently and reliably deploying multi-agent reinforcement learning controllers in heterogeneous building environments.

title: Integrated Life Cycle Assessment and Net-Zero Pathway Modeling for Sand Cores in Aluminum Semi-Permanent Mold (SPM) Casting: Integrating Endpoint Damage and Alternative Scenarios
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Integrated Life Cycle Assessment and Net-Zero Pathway Modeling for Sand Cores in Aluminum Semi-Permanent Mold (SPM) Casting: Integrating Endpoint Damage and Alternative Scenarios
detail.abstract: In response to the strengthening of global environmental regulations, the aluminum casting industry is actively attempting to replace conventional organic binders with inorganic alternatives. However, there is a lack of multi-dimensional evaluations regarding the impact of combining inorganic binders with chemical regeneration processes on the overall environmental load and its trade-offs. This study conducted a 'cradle-to-gate' Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) targeting sand cores used in aluminum semi-permanent mold (SPM) casting. Based on this, the environmental feasibility and pathways to achieving net-zero upon introducing inorganic binders and chemical regeneration systems were analyzed.,The evaluation results identified the primary aluminum ingot as the dominant hotspot, accounting for over 90% of the total Global Warming Potential (GWP). Despite fundamentally blocking hazardous gas emissions, the inorganic binder-based chemical regeneration system showed limitations in slightly worsening the climate change and ionizing radiation midpoint indicators due to massive power consumption. However, the integrated damage assessment applying the ReCiPe Endpoint (H) methodology revealed that the inorganic system reduced human health damage by 11.1% by eliminating carcinogenic substances. Furthermore, it proved its inherent eco-friendliness by improving the overall environmental damage Single Score from the conventional 0.6706 Pt to 0.6429 Pt, representing an approximately 4.1% improvement.,Furthermore, multi-dimensional alternative scenarios were modeled to overcome the power dependency and raw material limitations of the chemical regeneration process. The results showed that an optimized scenario combining an 80% substitution with aluminum scrap, a transition to a solar photovoltaic (Solar PV) grid, and an ultrasonic-assisted washing process caused the system's total GWP to plummet to 6.6 kg CO2-eq. This study proves that an approximately 80% reduction in carbon emissions compared to the baseline is possible when material, energy, and process innovations converge, moving beyond single-process improvements.

title: The Benefits of Regulatory Integration: Evidence from the 2024 U.S. Presidential Election
affiliations: East Carolina University and Texas State University

detail.title: The Benefits of Regulatory Integration: Evidence from the 2024 U.S. Presidential Election
detail.abstract: The stock market’s reaction to the 2024 U.S. presidential election presented an exogenous shock to expected regulatory integration. We use this shock to assess the distribution of expected benefits of that integration. We document that firms with greater exposure to regulatory separation, defined and quantified as exposure to multiple regulatory agencies, experienced higher abnormal returns during the election window as the stock market anticipated the benefits of the incoming Trump administration’s regulatory integration push to disproportionately accrue to those firms. Critically, the anticipated benefits of regulatory integration, and therefore estimated costs of regulatory separation, concentrate among underperforming firms and those with below-median market power. Regulatory theory of Laffont and Martimort (1999) suggests that separation reduces regulatory collusion and capture and therefore helps regulation act as a check on firms with the most resources to exploit market failures. Our findings contradict this view and suggest compliance costs as the true burden of regulatory separation.
